text:
I declare open this hearing of the Environment and Communications Legislation Committee of the Senate into the 2026-27 budget estimates. I begin by acknowledging the traditional custodians of the land on which we meet and pay our respects to Elders past, present and emerging. At this point I would like to speak on behalf of the committee in sending our thoughts to our colleague the member for Indi, Dr Helen Haines MP, her family, her team and her community as she continues to recover in hospital. The attack against Dr Haines on Monday last week was horrific. I know that many, including myself, have come to this place distressed by that attack and also in shock at what has happened to our colleague and our friend. Helen remains in all of our thoughts. Dr Haines is much loved as a colleague here, a strong advocate for her community in Indi and a robust, civil and kind participant in our democracy. Contributions will be made in the House of Representatives today from 10 am, and the committee will suspend to enable senators to attend the first of these statements as a mark of respect for Dr Haines. I do note that there are a number of matters under investigation by Victoria Police, the Australian Federal Police and ASIO, and I ask senators to please be mindful of this during hearings. Dr Haines is known to all of us as a person of integrity, of warmth, of kindness and as someone who conducts public debate in a robust but respectful manner. As chair, I will be taking this context into our hearings here today and tomorrow, and I'm sure my fellow senators join with me in this spirit and with Dr Haines in our minds.

The committee has fixed Thursday, 17 December 2026 as the date for the return of answers to questions on notice. Before I commence today's proceedings with corporate matters and general questions of the Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water portfolio, in an unusual move, we are in a position this morning to release the Australian Energy Infrastructure Commissioner from their attendance at estimates today, and they go with our thanks. We now proceed to corporate matters and general questions of the Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water portfolio.

Under standing order 26, the committee must take all evidence in public session. This includes answers to questions on notice. I remind all witnesses that, in giving evidence to the committee, they are protected by parliamentary privilege. It is unlawful for anyone to threaten or disadvantage a witness on account of evidence given to a committee, and such action may be treated by the Senate as a contempt. It is also a contempt to give false or misleading evidence to the Senate. The Senate has endorsed the following test of relevance of questions at estimates hearings. Any questions going to the operations or financial positions of the departments and agencies which are seeking funds in the estimates are relevant questions for the purposes of estimates hearings. I remind officers that the Senate has resolved that there are no areas in connection with the expenditure of public funds where any person has a discretion to withhold details or explanations from the parliament or its committees unless the parliament has expressly provided otherwise. The Senate has resolved also that an officer of a department of the Commonwealth shall not be asked to give opinions on matters of policy and shall be given reasonable opportunity to refer questions asked of the officer to superior officers or to a minister. This resolution does not preclude questions asking for explanations of policies or factual questions about when or how policies were adopted. Witnesses are reminded of the Senate order specifying the process by which a claim of public interest immunity should be raised. I incorporate the public interest immunity statement into Hansard.

The extract read as follows—

Public interest immunity claims

That the Senate—

(a) notes that ministers and officers have continued to refuse to provide information to Senate committees without properly raising claims of public interest immunity as required by past resolutions of the Senate;

(b) reaffirms the principles of past resolutions of the Senate by this order, to provide ministers and officers with guidance as to the proper process for raising public interest immunity claims and to consolidate those past resolutions of the Senate;

(c) orders that the following operate as an order of continuing effect:

(1) If:

(a) a Senate committee, or a senator in the course of proceedings of a committee, requests information or a document from a Commonwealth department or agency; and

(b) an officer of the department or agency to whom the request is directed believes that it may not be in the public interest to disclose the information or document to the committee, the officer shall state to the committee the ground on which the officer believes that it may not be in the public interest to disclose the information or document to the committee, and specify the harm to the public interest that could result from the disclosure of the information or document.

(2) If, after receiving the officer's statement under paragraph (1), the committee or the senator requests the officer to refer the question of the disclosure of the information or document to a responsible minister, the officer shall refer that question to the minister.

(3) If a minister, on a reference by an officer under paragraph (2), concludes that it would not be in the public interest to disclose the information or document to the committee, the minister shall provide to the committee a statement of the ground for that conclusion, specifying the harm to the public interest that could result from the disclosure of the information or document.

(4) A minister, in a statement under paragraph (3), shall indicate whether the harm to the public interest that could result from the disclosure of the information or document to the committee could result only from the publication of the information or document by the committee, or could result, equally or in part, from the disclosure of the information or document to the committee as in camera evidence.

(5) If, after considering a statement by a minister provided under paragraph (3), the committee concludes that the statement does not sufficiently justify the withholding of the information or document from the committee, the committee shall report the matter to the Senate.

(6) A decision by a committee not to report a matter to the Senate under paragraph (5) does not prevent a senator from raising the matter in the Senate in accordance with other procedures of the Senate.

(7) A statement that information or a document is not published, or is confidential, or consists of advice to, or internal deliberations of, government, in the absence of specification of the harm to the public interest that could result from the disclosure of the information or document, is not a statement that meets the requirements of paragraph (1) or (4).

(8) If a minister concludes that a statement under paragraph (3) should more appropriately be made by the head of an agency, by reason of the independence of that agency from ministerial direction or control, the minister shall inform the committee of that conclusion and the reason for that conclusion, and shall refer the matter to the head of the agency, who shall then be required to provide a statement in accordance with paragraph (3).

(d) requires the Procedure Committee to review the operation of this order and report to the Senate by 20 August 2009.

(13 May 2009 J.1941)

(Extract, Senate Standing Orders)

text:
Briefly, yes. Firstly, I know I speak on behalf of everyone in the department in expressing my shock at recent events in Wangaratta. Our thoughts and hopes for a speedy recovery are with the member for Indi, her family, her staff and the community. There are many things that the department has achieved since the last hearings that I could cover, but I wanted particularly to focus these introductory remarks on the recent pre-COP event in Fiji and the departmental staff who travelled to support it. The starting point is straightforward. The Australian government decided to help host and fund a pre-COP in Fiji in partnership with Pacific nations. Holding the event in Fiji created logistical challenges, but, once the government had made that decision, our responsibility as public servants was to deliver it well, use public resources responsibly and achieve the government's objectives. That meant considerably more than sending an Australian delegation to a conference. We were helping to deliver the practicalities of a major international event in a foreign country while also pursuing important climate and diplomatic objectives for Australia and the Pacific. The operational task included security, venues and suppliers, transport, protocol, media and arrangements for leaders and delegates. As reported, the event management costs alone associated with this effort were of the order of $20 million. Along with these logistical tasks, our negotiators, policy officials and Pacific teams had to deliver the substantive program and engage with governments and international partners on the issues that matter to our nation and the Pacific ahead of COP31.

We assessed the effort required to do both: to deliver the event successfully and to achieve its broader objectives. On that basis, I approved the travel to Fiji of 51 departmental officials for operational delivery and 48 supporting negotiations and engagement. My decision needs to be understood in the context of the task the government gave us, the roles those staff performed and what they delivered. From 5 to 8 October in Fiji, more than 4,000 people from over 100 countries participated, including 53 leaders and ministers. There were 135 events across four venues, with more than 130 international journalists covering proceedings. But the purpose was not simply to stage a large and well-run event. There were two broader objectives: firstly, to put Pacific priorities at the centre of the international climate discussion and help shape the agenda towards COP31 in Turkiye. This included keeping 1.5 degrees within reach, adaptation, climate finance and the ocean-climate relationship. Secondly, to strengthen Australia's relationships with Pacific neighbours by bringing the international community into the region to engage directly with Pacific perspectives and priorities. I believe those objectives were met, and I am very proud of what our people achieved with our partners in Fiji and across the Pacific.

text: That's indeed right. As the secretary said, around $20 million for the event management company, which is essentially the hub around which we designed the delivery of the event. The event management company supported all of the aspects of the operational planning and delivery of the event. That's the structural build—things like the physical infrastructure needed to host the meeting, the fitting out of venues, setting up of security infrastructure and then specialist services like simultaneous translation, audiovisual hardware and technical production, media facilities and the technical workforce necessary to put on the event. That also includes some transport services, but the transport program was delivered in partnership with the government of Fiji. Similarly with security: again, delivered in partnership with the government of Fiji. The $34.6 million also includes $2 million to put on host broadcaster services, which was a necessary component to ensure the proceedings were made publicly available in terms of the screening of the meetings. There were also some additional costs associated with procurement support, commercial advice, readiness support, probity—those kinds of technical matters.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Sorry, what was that last hotel?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The Radisson Blu: $19,866. The Crowne Plaza: $995,650. The Fiji Gateway Hotel: $37,000. The Tanoa International: $94,157. The Novotel: $90,850. The Tokatoka Resort: $102,749. The Wyndham Garden: $172,890. The Sebel: $313,595. The Nalagi Hotel: $88,710. The Grand West Villas: $17,985.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: How many nights of accommodation is this for in total?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I couldn't tell you in terms of the information I have in front of me, because these venues were used to support delegates. They were also used to support workforce accommodation. There's a range of arrangements. Delegates might have been on the ground for three or four days. Some of the workforce were there for longer. This was also to support the Fijian workforce. I would have to take on notice a breakdown with respect to nights.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: If you could, please, and if you could come back to us today, if you can, that would be appreciated. What was the cost of ground transport?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I don't have a ground transport total for you, in part because Fiji was responsible for delivering transport. We provided support for it in terms of a range of elements, including providing some operational and logistical support, but transport services in the main were provided by the government of Fiji.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You've mentioned that there might be some reimbursement from delegates and others. How much money is it expected that the government will be spending? What's the actual cost that's estimated, based on agreements that have been made for reimbursement?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I've given you the outer bound of the total accommodation and venue cost. I cannot give you an accurate indication of how much will be recouped from that amount.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Can you give me a ballpark?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I can't, I'm afraid, not until that has been reconciled.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Who's agreed to repay their costs?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Again, I don't have that information in front of me. The government of Australia retained accommodation across a range of venues in order to ensure there was going to be ample accommodation for delegates attending. That's the arrangement we entered into. The reconciliation with respect to who used those rooms and for what length is still being resolved with the venues themselves, and I cannot give you an accurate indication.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: When will that reconciliation process conclude?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I suspect it will probably take about another month or so, according to our technical people, but I certainly do not have it now.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What was the cost of catering?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Again, catering was absorbed in venue costs in the main, so that's largely included in that amount that I've provided to you.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The $20 million?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: In part in the $20 million and also in the $8 million for accommodation and venues.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Can you give me a breakdown, though, in general terms? If catering is paid for out of that $20 million component as well as out of the accommodation component, what roughly are you talking about in terms of catering costs?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I can take on notice the amounts that were potentially allocated for the day-to-day catering through the course of the meetings, if that's useful. I don't have that information in front of me, because it was absorbed in the larger contract.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, but you must know, in terms of the breakdown of the contract, how that $20 million was spent. Can you please run us through the breakdown of that $20 million?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We had arrangements in place with venues, including the Sheraton, where the principal pre-COP was held. In securing the use of the conference facilities, catering was packaged into that arrangement so that the provision of morning tea, afternoon tea and lunch was included in that package. I do not have a disaggregated amount. It was part of the conference package.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: If morning and afternoon tea and lunch were included in the accommodation package—that is the $8.4 million—how much additional money was spent on catering, including alcohol, both out of that package and also the $20 million? Do you have a breakdown for alcohol consumption?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I don't. There were two events that were held which the government of Fiji hosted that we supported. One was a welcome event that was hosted by Fijian ministers, and that event cost approximately $8,900. I do not have an amount for alcohol. There was a thanksgiving reception that the Fijian minister for climate hosted at the Sheraton that had an estimated cost of around $70,000.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: For context, the total catering cost for the G20 in 2014 under Prime Minister Abbott was over $1 million.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You're not suggesting for a second that the G20 and APEC are of the same standing as the Fiji and Tuvalu conferences, are you, Senator Watt? I just want to be very clear about that. How many world leaders attended the APEC event, and who were they? How many attended?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think they're all—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Close to 20.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think they're all important events, Senator Smith.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Not of the scale.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I haven't finished.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: With all due respect, not of the scale of APEC and the G20. We're talking a very different set of circumstances here.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think they are all important events, and I can only assume—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Not of the same scale.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I can only assume, then, Senator Smith—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Not of the same scale.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: If I can finish? I can only assume, Senator Smith, that's why the hotel cost for the G20 was more than double what was spent on venues and accommodation for this event, and why the hotel and accommodation costs for APEC were more than double what was spent. I guess that's consistent with what you're saying.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: With your comprehensive set of notes, Minister, you might want to share with us which world leaders attended APEC and the G20 compared to which world leaders attended the conference that we're interrogating.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm happy to get that information for you, Senator Smith, but I don't think the only test of whether an event is important or not is how many world leaders attend.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think it is.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Can I finish?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think it is. I think it's a very important test of credibility.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You're entitled to your view. Our government also thinks an important test of whether an event is worthwhile is whether it is something that is strongly supported and sought by the leaders in our very region, a region that we have a massive strategic and national security interest in supporting. Any leader in the Pacific will tell you that the single biggest challenge they face is climate change. Some of us don't want to go back to the days where ministers in a government were making jokes about water lapping at their doors. We actually think those issues are important.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think your APEC comparison only takes you a very short distance.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: As I say, I can only assume that's why more than double the cost was incurred in hosting APEC and the G20, and that is, of course, in 2007 and 2014 dollars.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Probably four times as many world leaders attending. You might be able to bring that information to the table today.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: As I say, you might think what is important is numbers of world leaders attending. What our government thinks is important is working with our nearest region, where we have a huge national security and strategic interest and where, the last time the coalition was in power, we saw the Solomon Islands sign a security deal with China. We have a different approach.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I suspect the APEC comparison will only take you a very short distance, and I suspect the criteria for success of the conference changed when world leaders decided they weren't going to come.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I know the coalition doesn't believe in climate change and has abandoned its commitment to net zero, which means that you've abandoned the Pacific with the greatest concern they have. I was in Papua New Guinea last week with other ministers in the annual talks that we have with ministers. The single biggest issue that was being discussed there was the impact of El Nino on Papua New Guinea right now. I saw it for myself. The coalition can continue to put its head in the sand if they wish, ignore the impacts of climate change and disrespect the Pacific, as we saw from numerous coalition figures through pre-COP. That is not what we are going to do as a government.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Minister, your government is destroying this country with your energy policies, and Australians are suffering and paying the price. We are not going to take a lecture because of your shockingly flawed policies.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That's your view.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Let's come back to corporate matters in the department. I think we've strayed away from that a little bit.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Staying with the matter of accommodation expenses, am I right to assume that, as part of the reconciliation or acquittal process, you would have kept a measurement or a record of the utilisation of rooms that were booked or surrendered during the process of confirming delegate accommodation and arrangements?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That's right, although that was done in conjunction with the hotels themselves, obviously, which managed the rooms. We had arrangements in place with each of the hotels, and the hotels then worked to allocate those rooms to delegates. We were obviously in contact with the hotels. The reconciliation process obviously requires us to engage with the hotels and, in some instances, with delegations.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Am I right to assume that there was 100 per cent utilisation of all of the rooms across all of those venues?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That I don't know. I would have to check for you. I would be surprised if it was 100 per cent, but let me check for you.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: They were half utilised?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I wouldn't speculate. I don't know. I think the vast majority of rooms were utilised, but I couldn't give you a percentage.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What I can tell you, Senator Smith, is that, when APEC was hosted in 2007 under Prime Minister Howard, 6,000 delegates and 1,500 journalists were forecast to attend. When the event was held, the final number was well short, with only 4,000 delegates and fewer than 1,000 journalists showing up. The coalition were forced to release more than 2,000 luxury hotel rooms in central Sydney back to the market.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: And how many world leaders? You've got a comprehensive set of notes, Senator Watt. How many world leaders?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm sure that the G20—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: How many world leaders?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm sure that the G20—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: How many world leaders?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Can I finish?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: How many world leaders?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senators, come to order, please.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Australia is not—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson, please don't talk over the top of me when I've called 'order'. I have started today with the hope that we would conduct this in a way that was civil and we would engage in the questions—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It is civil, just to be clear, Chair. It is civil and good humoured.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Smith, before everyone jumps in, it is civil. I am not saying you are being uncivil, but both you and the minister are talking over the top of each other relatively constantly. I appreciate the strength of your relationship, but I also have, in my experience, come to see this committee very quickly accelerate from what is a civil but nevertheless slightly fractious exchange into something that is less than civil. I am simply trying to keep that in order. When I do so, I would appreciate everyone in the room coming to order so I can do that. I am not suggesting otherwise.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Civil, good humoured and good natured. Mr Higgins, on notice, if you could provide us some information around the utilisation of rooms across those venues, that would be much appreciated.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: And we could compare that to the 2,000 luxury hotel rooms in central Sydney released back to the market.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm looking forward to the list of world leaders.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It must have been quite a few of them who didn't show up if 2,000 luxury hotel rooms were released back to the market.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: World leaders—the number of world leaders?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think world leaders probably stay in luxury hotel rooms. It was probably within the 2,000.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Or perhaps they economised with their delegations.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm glad you mentioned economising, because, with this event, ministers and advisers and all departmental officials travelled economy fares to Fiji, and only where strictly necessary for security and operational purposes did ministers, officials and advisers stay onsite at the main venue. The vast majority of staff—around 75—stayed offsite in more modest accommodation, saving up to $166 per room per night.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'd hardly regard that as a virtue. That's my expectation.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm making the point that your expectation was fulfilled.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The government has met my expectation. If it were any different, I wouldn't regard it as a virtue.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Sure.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That's my expectation.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm glad that we met your expectation on this point. The point being made is that efforts were made to economise.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Civil and good natured, yes. Thank you, Mr Higgins.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Can I pick up on the world leaders who did attend the pre-COP. Minister Bowen said on 5 October 2026, 'This is the first pre-COP where we've invited world leaders.' The government kept that invite list secret. Can we please understand how many world leaders were invited, how many attended and who they were.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I can give you a list of those who attended the Tuvalu visit and participated in the leaders plenary that was held in Fiji. I can't give you a list of those who were invited. That was a matter for the Prime Minister's office. It was managed by PM&C and DFAT, so I'd have to refer you to them.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Higgins, firstly, could you set out which world leaders attended the Tuvalu and Fiji components please.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Prime Minister Albanese, Prime Minister Feleti Teo of Tuvalu, the Prime Minister of Fiji, the Prime Minister of Cook Islands, the President of Timor-Leste, the President of Palau, the Prime Minister of Papua New Guinea, the President of Mauritius, the President of New Caledonia, the Prime Minister of Niue, the Prime Minister of the Solomon Islands, the Prime Minister of Tonga, the Prime Minister of Vanuatu and the President of Nauru. There were other senior representatives in attendance. The Asian Development Bank was represented by its president.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Can I stay on world leaders. There are no non-Pacific world leaders?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We think Pacific leaders matter too, Senator Henderson.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: So do I, Minister. Please don't reflect on me. I'm asking Mr Higgins. There were no non-Pacific world leaders?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Mauritius and Timor-Leste were both represented.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Not part of the Pacific, Senator Henderson.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Part of the broader region.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think you're right: Mauritius is in quite a different region.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That's correct. Just a couple of things: the funding for pre-COP was drawn from an overall allocation by this government for COP related events. That overall allocation—and this is on the public record already—is $147.8 million. As I say, that's not just for pre-COP; that's for COP related events in general. The funding for this came from that bucket of funds.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What was that figure again?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: $147.8 million. But, to your point, Senator Brown, you're correct; the cost of pre-COP was fully funded by savings generated by this government out of a $500 million coalition-era program known as the strategic international partnership investment stream. Essentially, this was a program that was invented by then minister Angus Taylor as the energy minister to persuade the Pacific to overlook the fact that, under the former government, Australia was consistently voting with countries like Russia on climate matters at COP events. The then Morrison government, including minister Taylor, created the $500 million Strategic International Partnership Investment Stream to persuade countries, as I say, to overlook our voting behaviour as a country. The cost of pre-COP has been fully funded from that saving. I can only assume that the coalition, given its demands for savings by this government, would support the fact that savings were found to fund the pre-COP event.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

text: As you would recall, Senator Brown, during the time of the former coalition government, Pacific leaders were dismayed at the approach of then government towards climate change matters. The most celebrated example, of course, is what Mr Dutton would have referred to as a joke but what was a really offensive statement towards the Pacific. Pacific leaders were dismayed. Australia under the former government, as I say, was consistently voting with countries like Russia at COP and other climate change events. The then government created this $500 million program, which would have been able to be used to fund particular programs in the Pacific. Our government has not needed to persuade Pacific countries of our record on climate change, because we are working with them. We were able to fund this event by removing those funds from that coalition-era program. I think you called it a 'reprioritisation', and that would be a fair way to describe it.

A lot of repair work has needed to be done in Australia's interest.

portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Kaiser, is it correct that this department is responsible for organising the pre-COP as opposed to the invitations?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Aspects of pre-COP, yes. As has been explained in earlier testimony, we weren't involved in the organising of the Tuvalu visit but, broadly, matters that occurred in Fiji were our responsibility.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Right, so you'd be booking accommodation—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, for those that accepted the invitation.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: If the President of America was coming, you would have to have different arrangements than if you were just having the foreign ministers?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The question was about our knowledge of who was invited.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, my question to you is: when you were deciding on the location and booking accommodation, you would have planned a different event if you had thought that you were having world leaders as opposed to foreign ministers?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Based on the acceptance of invitations not issued by us.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It's like planning any event. You book the venue based on who you think is coming, what their requirements would be and the calibre of the guests, but you had no input into that. You just blindly booked a venue and then said, 'If the President comes, we'll have to book out half the island, and, if he doesn't, then we'll just have foreign leaders.' Is that the sort of approach it was? 'We'll just book an event, book a location, and then whoever turns up, we'll sort it out after that.'

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We were involved in booking accommodation on the basis of some of those costs being returned if the accommodation was taken up by other nations. We made ample provision for those who may show up on the basis of reimbursable costs.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: So you contemplated the idea that you might have had world leaders. You may have had world leaders—you didn't, but you may have had world leaders—and so you planned for that eventuality. You must have kicked around a list of names of people who might turn up or who you'd hope would turn up.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not sure what relevance the names would have.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It's the capacity of the department to make good planning and decisions, because we're worried about the egregious waste of—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: If you'll allow me—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, I won't allow you just yet. Let me finish my question, please.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What is the point of me making an answer?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, let me finish my question, please. My question is: we are concerned about the egregious expenditure of money on this event that then didn't attract the world leaders that the environment minister promised would come. We're trying to understand: was there even the most basic level of planning? 'We're going to plan for world leaders to come', or 'Are we just planning for the local blokes to come from the local community?' It's a very different event. You would have planned it very differently, but I'm getting an assertion that you didn't know who was invited, you didn't know who was coming, you just booked out a local resort and hoped that it would all work out, and you spent a hell of a lot of money doing so.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I will deal with that question. There may be more that officials can provide in terms of what were the arrangements. However, it is not unusual, in organising these events, for contingencies to be put in place for a large number of delegates from countries to attend. In 2007, when Prime Minister Howard hosted APEC, the forecast was for 6,000 delegates. The final number was well short of expectations. Thousands of Sydney hotel rooms had to be released. That is not unusual. I make no criticism of those APEC arrangements. I just say that it's not unusual. In relation to the G20, it's very similar. When you say 'the local blokes coming', I can't help but think that question reflects a—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, it doesn't. I'm trying to understand whether or not you thought that it was—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You must allow me to finish my answers. You must allow me to finish.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You don't let me finish my questions, so—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I had started to answer your question, and you provided an additional question. I can't help but think that the coalition has not learnt the national security lesson that should have been learnt following 2019 to 2022. Senator Canavan said just a few weeks ago, 'I don't look as silly as Anthony Albanese and Chris Bowen in those stupid Hawaiian shirts.' Can you imagine that there is any utility in being derogatory about a national dress? There are no serious people; there are no—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senators and Minister, just one moment, please. I have let this go because it has been done in relatively good humour, but I think we're at risk of going off the rails for a moment. Let's just bring this back to the classic way that this works best, which is questions and answers. Minister, I think you're coming to the end of that, and then maybe to officials in response to Senator McDonald's questions, and then we'll move on.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Serious issues require serious people saying serious things when it goes to our security and resilience in the region, and there is a lack of seriousness about the approach being taken in relation to this set of issues. That's all I say.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator McDonald, you had a question, I think, that you had put. Did the officials at the table want to answer or add to that answer?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Can I just provide some further context, because I do think it's important? We weren't able to answer this before, but in terms of the broader representation of leaders and ministers, there were 53 leaders and ministers, around 600 official delegates from 61 countries and 3,199 participants as part of the stakeholder program representing over 100 countries. Importantly, when we are talking about the Tuvalu component, it did include the president of the Asian Development Bank, the executive director of the Green Climate Fund, the secretary-general of the Pacific Islands Forum, the executive secretary of the UNFCCC, the deputy secretary-general of the UN, Amina Mohammed, as well as the former prime minister of Australia and chair of the Wellcome Trust, Julia Gillard. Again, there were a number of other ministerial and senior representatives, including the COP31 President-designate, Minister Kurum, the minister from Antigua and Barbuda, the minister from Barbados, the European Commissioner for Climate Action—
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I can do that, but I also wanted just to continue, because it did include the Minister of Foreign Affairs from Nepal, for example, the Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate from India and the Minister of Environment from Indonesia. I do think that broader perspective of who was actually represented at both leader and senior ministerial level is quite significant for the complexity of the event, but it also goes to—
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We're running an hour over—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That's a matter for you. I just say officials are entitled to answer the questions no matter how inconvenient to the Liberal Party they might be.

portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

I'm very happy for my colleague Mr Higgins to talk more about that contingency planning and security.

portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We're under a lot of time pressure. In relation to the planning concerning the prospective list of world leaders, if you could please put that on notice, including correspondence between your department and PM&C and DFAT—planning in relation to the possible attendance of world leaders such as the US President, the Prime Minister of the UK and other world leaders. I say that, Ms Munro, because your own minister, Minister Bowen, said on 5 October, 'This is the first pre-COP where we have invited world leaders', and yet the government is keeping this list secret. It is not unreasonable that we would seek the details of who was invited.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: In relation to the President of the United States, I don't know. The United States is not in the Paris Agreement. I don't know what that means in terms of invitations that are extended. It's really a question for Prime Minister and Cabinet to answer. I have no knowledge of which invitations were issued. I have no knowledge of when they were issued. I have no knowledge of the process that was engaged in there. This line agency's job is to book the rooms and to deliver the conference. That's as far as that goes.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

Confusingly, invoices relating to Ms Higgins's travel were filed by the department. Was Ms Higgins's travel—that's accommodation and flights—paid for by the taxpayer in any way?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
