agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: If I could perhaps answer some of the questions on the New England REZ. You've quoted from the draft ISP, which was released in December 2025, and we've had a final since then, released in June 2026. As you say, the New England REZ is now an anticipated project under the 2026 ISP. The way the categorisation of projects works is that AEMO has a set of criteria that it applies to projects. To be a committed project, you need to meet five criteria: site acquisition, components ordered, planning approvals, finance completion and construction timing set. To be an anticipated project, which is what the New England REZ is in the final ISP, you need to be in the process of meeting at least three of those five criteria. Part of why—
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Three of the five, yes. I apologise; I don't have the appendices with me, so I can't tell you which of the five the New England REZ has met. But, looking at the footnote, it looks as if between draft and final the New England REZ was brought into the New South Wales regulatory framework, into their energy roadmap, and that changes the way the project is approved. I think that might be the reason, but I can't be definitive on that. Just in terms of consultation, the process of releasing a draft and then a final is in fact to do that consultation. AEMO then takes submissions on the draft ISP and takes that information into account when it's developing its final ISP.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

text: It's public knowledge that they're distorting. They even had it in their own press releases that coal is cheaper.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I understand that it's fashionable amongst One Nation party representatives to denigrate the work of Australian scientists in our premier national science organisation, and that is the only way that you continue to make those kinds of claims. We know that is the case. We rely upon the experts, not the social media posters and the cartoonists. We rely upon the evidence. The evidence is very clear, and it does require cooperation between Commonwealth and state governments to deliver these projects. In my own portfolio area, delivering wind and solar generation in the great state of Queensland to support industrial jobs in Central Queensland required the cooperation of the private sector, the Commonwealth and the state government. We will keep doing that. If in New South Wales the framework that they adopt is through the renewable energy zones, that is the framework that we will work with, because that is in the interests of lower-cost electricity, industrial jobs and blue-collar communities. We're about practical action to deliver for them, not slogans that would destroy those communities and destroy those jobs, which is where you're coming from.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Minister, you realise that solar and wind are coming unravelled around the world now, but you're still maintaining that line?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I will need to move the call. Senator Pocock.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I have some questions for program 1.2. Are you aware of reports that there have been large and unexplained releases of methane from Chevron's Gorgon facility?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We are aware of media reports over the last couple of days about releases from Chevron's Gorgon project. My understanding is that's a matter for the state regulator.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: So you don't have any details about it?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, not within my division.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: If I look at the estimates program, program 1.2, 'Reduce Australia's greenhouse gas emissions', how on earth is this program going to be successful if we don't know about a reportedly massive unexplained release of methane over the last year or so?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: A facility of that size would, from a Commonwealth regulatory perspective, be reporting under the NGER legislation, which is administered by the Clean Energy Regulator. They do the operational elements of that. I can come back to you with further detail on notice, if you like, on their particular obligations, but I suspect that your questions are probably best put to the Clean Energy Regulator with regard to any reporting if there's a particular unplanned or otherwise venting event. My colleague's comments would also be accurate: there would be state based regulation that also captured that, if it's an unplanned event.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I guess my question was: how are we going to reduce Australia's greenhouse gas emissions if the federal department doesn't even know about huge methane emissions?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm very happy to talk to you about how the policy framework works to reduce methane emissions, but we took your initial question as being about there having been some unplanned venting event and who the notification obligations related to. My best answer for you is that's probably the Clean Energy Regulator, who are appearing later today, as is my understanding, as well as state regulators. With regard to your question about how we are going to reduce emissions from these sorts of facilities, obviously the Australian government has a legislative commitment to get to net zero, a series of interim targets and a policy framework that sits under that. Chevron, clearly, given its size, is regulated under the Safeguard Mechanism. That applies, as you know, declining baselines that they have to meet over time from a net emissions reduction perspective. So, if there is an event over the course of their operations that means their emissions are higher than anticipated, there are a series of controls that apply under the Safeguard Mechanism that require them, over time, to comply with their baseline.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You told me a minute ago that it was a state issue, but the safeguard is federal.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The safeguard is federal; that's correct. Just to be really clear, we originally took your question to be, 'We're hearing reports of a large venting event. Are you aware of that?' That spoke to us as a notification piece. There would be notification obligations that required the facility to report to either federal or state regulators. Your second question was about how we are encouraging those facilities to reduce their emissions over time. The Safeguard Mechanism is the primary mechanism, and it relies on their annual reports rather than moment-in-time reports. Each year they will report on their emissions and how they're meeting their declining baselines on a net basis.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: To your knowledge, has Chevron made a report about these leaks?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I have a similar understanding to my colleague here, given that we're not the regulators under the Safeguard Mechanism or the state based legislation.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, but you are responsible for reducing Australia's greenhouse gas emissions.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That is correct. As I said, we administer the Safeguard Mechanism, which relies on annual reporting, not day-by-day reporting. As I said, there are different roles that the different agencies play in the Commonwealth.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Are you aware of a report from Chevron?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm aware of the media reporting, but if they are obliged to report an event it would likely be to the Clean Energy Regulator, which is a different agency from those officials sitting before you.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You don't talk to them about this stuff?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: There's a range of things we talk to them about on a daily basis. I haven't personally spoken to them about this.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Has anyone here? Does anyone know if Chevron have reported this to you?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The Clean Energy Regulator appears before the committee later in the schedule. You could perhaps ask them.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I guess I just find it—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: They are the regulator. In this space, we are primarily a policy agency. There's a whole range of regulators in the portfolio family, if you want to call it that, which have different responsibilities. As has been suggested, this may be a question for the Clean Energy Regulator.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'll come back to them. You look at what's happening with climate at the moment, and, looking at what Data Desk is estimating, there could have been around 16,000 tonnes of methane leaked into the atmosphere. The impact of that over 20 years is the equivalent of putting more than half a million additional cars on the road. So I come to ask about outcome 1.2, 'Reduce Australia's greenhouse gas emissions', and you don't even know if Chevron have reported this.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: There's a system in place for companies and facilities that are regulated under these pieces of legislation to do things like annual reporting for their annual obligations, which we can talk to. There's obviously a system for them to notify the relevant regulators under different legislation, as appropriate. I really encourage you to ask the Clean Energy Regulator about whether they have been notified yet. The point that I would choose to make here about the scope and scale of these purported emissions is that we understand that the media reporting on this emission is probably drawing on what we would call top-down measurement systems, so things like satellites, flyovers and remote observations of methane. They are really useful but expensive technologies for understanding where leaks might be occurring. It's much more problematic to use them for really accurate measurement of how much methane has been released in any particular event. There are many hundreds of different kinds of sensors mounted on many different kinds of platforms, and they use lots of different methodologies in terms of how they calculate things. That's why we've got the expert panel on methane emissions reductions to look into these technologies.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: But, Mr Hutchinson, as you would know better than most, here in Australia we are woefully behind when it comes to everything outside of underground mining and methane measurement. We're way behind. But that's a different issue. It seems to me all the experts are saying, 'From the satellite imagery and from the flyovers, this is a huge event', and DCCEEW isn't even aware of it apart from media reporting.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I wouldn't characterise us as being woefully behind in terms of how we measure and manage methane in this country. We have some of the most sophisticated methods globally for accurately measuring methane. Under NGERS, our method 2 is globally recognised as one of the most stringent ways you can get accurate, repeatable measurements of methane. We're really interested in these top-down ways of measuring that we assume these media reports are based on, and that's why we've got former Chief Scientist Cathy Foley heading up a panel of experts to look into how these different technologies could be used to augment and improve our systems over time. It is a vast array of technologies and approaches. They are going to spend two and a half years in total looking at that. We're now about nine months away, I believe, from their final report. They've just released an interim report on it. I would definitely commend that piece of research to you, to look into whether these systems are useful for quantifying methane leaks.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Minister, what do you have to say about Chevron and their methane leaks? Clearly they're not a good corporate citizen if this is the way that they are treating Australia and the public.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I've just reviewed the article that you've referred to, which appears to be related to independent satellite monitoring of the facility and, I think, an assertion that in late August it recorded an average emission rate of about 7.8 tonnes of methane an hour. You used a figure earlier; I didn't quite catch it. It appears, just from reading the article, that there is not a settled approach; maybe there is with the regulator in Western Australia. As the officials outlined to you, the department's job here is as a policy lead. The regulators, in this case the CER and the Western Australian regulator, have a function to discharge to deliver on the integrity of the policy measures. That requires annual emissions measurement and, I assume, particularly at the state level, some more granular compliance work. This will be the subject of discussions between the regulators and Chevron. They will come up with a settled approach: is there more than anticipated? Is it a result of some engineering defect, or what are the circumstances here? Nobody in this room knows. There are stringent rules in place to monitor emissions through the Safeguard Mechanism, and the CER is responsible for discharging that work. They will be able to answer those questions to the extent that they can. Officials here are not regulators; they are doing the policy work.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I accept that, Minister, but it's got to be someone's responsibility. We all pay the price for carbon in the atmosphere and climate change. It seems to me, when you look at what's happened with Santos up in Darwin and their leaking tank, thanks to ConocoPhillips, and how that was just not reported for years, and this one with Chevron, where we hear after the fact, that it is falling between the WA regulator and the Commonwealth.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, it hasn't fallen in between. There is the Clean Energy Regulator and the Western Australian regulator. They have duties to discharge. They will be discharging them. The Clean Energy Regulator will be here in minutes or hours time to answer questions about that. If there's some deficiency there, they will account for that issue. The officials who are here now are policy officials. They cannot and should not intervene, because that undermines the integrity of the compliance mechanism. That's what the Clean Energy Regulator is there to do. That's what the Western Australian system is there to do.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It's debatable.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I don't approach this set of issues with the cynicism that interjection evidences. I just say they are accountable for that work. They will be here to answer questions on that work. Officials here cannot help you on the individual ins and outs of an individual facility and its emissions. The story appears to say it's circa 7.8 tonnes of methane an hour. That is serious, because it's methane; it's got a bigger climate effect than CO2 does. But it's well within the scope of the regulator to deal with those questions, and they will no doubt be alerted by this discussion and come here able to answer those questions.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I wondered if we may now return to that question I was asking about diesel. Are you prepared now?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We've spoken with Treasury. I must apologise; you mentioned Treasury last time we were here in Senate estimates, when you put that question on notice. We didn't think that was the main line of inquiry. We thought your original question was just what we are seeing or projecting in terms of diesel use over time, and so we answered on that basis. I've reviewed it in the break. Apologies that we did not pick up on the issue that I am now clear you're asking about, which is that there is apparently, from your point of view, an inconsistency between what our numbers are saying and what Treasury's are saying. We've spoken with Treasury. We're in the process of working through that. We will come back to you on notice with a clear answer on that. They are both quite complex projection systems, and they're measuring different things in different ways, so we want to give you the best answer we can. I don't think I can do that justice now on the basis of an hour of work. So we'll do it on notice.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I've got quite a number of follow-up questions from that. I'll see if any of them are relevant in the absence of that clarity.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I do note that Treasury is on later this week. We will endeavour to do the best we can to provide you with additional clarity in that session, if that helps.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I might ask some questions about COP31; that requires a personnel change. Minister Bowen has said the COP31 presidency was a significant opportunity to lead on climate action, but since announcing your 2035 targets over a year ago only one meaningful policy, solar for industrial rooftops, has been announced. All indications are that COP31 could not only lack ambition; it could take the world backwards on climate action. What is the government doing to reverse this?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: COP31 and Australia's role there is obviously, as you said, the presidency of the negotiation. We have a very particular role. There are over 100 items and 60 mandates that need to be negotiated under the UNFCCC. Again, I'm just trying to explain what that role is, and then I'll come to your question. There are a number of reviews underway in terms of mitigation, the just transition goals, the agricultural work programs and how you scale up mitigation, ambition and implementation. There is the role that you take on in terms of how you progress these things under the UNFCCC and the Paris Agreement and, of course, what a country is responsible for as part of its own nationally determined contribution and the policies that come forward. To be fair, the context that Minister Bowen was talking about was absolutely the context of what's happening in the negotiations and, more generally, what's happening globally. I'm very happy to go into details about the—
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Can you share what announcements Australia plans to make at COP31?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think the answer to that question is: stay tuned for when the minister does that. I think you indicated earlier that there was one thing that the government had announced.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Solar for industrial rooftops.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think that has been announced since the 2035 target. At the same time as the 2035 target was announced, there was $5 billion from the Net Zero Fund and the National Reconstruction Fund to help industrial facilities decarbonise and scale up more renewables; $2 billion for the Clean Energy Finance Corporation to continue to drive investment in the electricity system; $1.1 billion to encourage more production of clean fuels here in Australia; and $40 million to accelerate the rollout of kerbside and fast EV charging. The list goes on. There's a very substantial set of announcements that the government made at the time of the 2035 target.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Is that still the Net Zero Fund that no money has been spent out of?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: All of these things take time.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The clock is ticking. While I've got you, Minister, can I ask: Australia is a signatory to the transition away from fossil fuels treaty signed in Belem. Can you explain how many new and expanded coal and gas projects this government has approved since signing that agreement?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I don't have those figures in front of me. I'm not sure, but I think that Senator Chisholm will probably be delighted to engage with you about those questions in resources estimates or in environment there might be an official who is able to answer that question. The framework that we're in does permit countries that have energy resources to export them, and countries are responsible for the emissions that they emit within their jurisdictions. That's the way that the framework works. If there were an effort to make it work any other way, it would fall apart and the world would go backwards in emissions terms. That's the truth of it. It's one thing to assert these propositions; it's another thing to deliver on them. Our job is to deliver on them.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That question was relating to how many new fossil fuel projects have been approved since 5 December.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: If we can come back to you, we will, but it's not primarily this department's work.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Do you expect that the government will approve the HBO expansion and the Browse project before COP31 is finished?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: All of those approval processes are a function of ministers exercising their role according to the law and on the basis of the submissions, material and facts that are provided to them. Ministers will discharge their obligations carefully, in the national interest and in accordance with the law. I don't think that Minister Watt in environment would be able to say much more than that. He is the responsible minister, but that's the way that this operates. It's not just ministers freelancing on these questions. There is a responsibility and a legal process.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm aware of that, but I'm just seeing if you can provide any information to some very concerned communities and climate groups about that, as well as the Pacific island leaders. I'm curious about this. At the recent pre-COP events—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: But if I did that, if I or Minister Watt or anybody else charged with these—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

text: These are questions on behalf of environmental and climate groups—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

text: responsibilities did that—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I do think I have the right to ask their questions, and I will continue to do that, Minister.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: it would open up court processes, it would open up vulnerabilities and it would undermine the integrity of the system.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It would annoy Woodside.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: There would be more problems, not fewer, as a result of that approach.

text: At the recent pre-COP events in Fiji and Tuvalu, did Pacific countries raise concern with Australian delegates about recent and upcoming fossil fuel projects?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I can answer that. There always are very honest and real conversations that happen with Pacific island countries. I won't go into the details, but we do have frank conversations with the Pacific on these matters.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You don't have to give me specifics of which country said what, but did they express concerns about upcoming decisions on fossil fuel projects in Australia?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think some ministers, from Vanuatu and others, are making those comments on the public record.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I might briefly return to the diesel question. Apologies for the personnel change again. I think there are some questions that I can ask on that in the absence of that fully formulated response. Are you seeing any diesel reduction at safeguard facilities so far, when they get paid $194 in fuel tax credits and only have to pay $35 for an ACCU?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We may need some additional colleagues at the table for that. Safeguard sits across two divisions, but I'm happy to make some comments. I think some of the initial numbers that we're finding on the safeguard are showing that the net emissions are coming down. The question of exactly where those emissions reductions are coming from, the split of on site and off site, is a further level.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Could you please repeat your question?
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Are you seeing any diesel reduction at safeguard facilities when they're getting paid $194 in fuel tax credits per tonne and only have to pay $35 for an ACCU?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: As Mr Hutchinson mentioned, the safeguard mechanism sets a level and it declines, but people then have flexibility about how they deploy different savings. There are facilities which are reducing diesel. In fact, last week I was visiting a Fortescue mine in the Pilbara, and they are well and truly on the way to getting rid of diesel outright from their facilities within the next 18 months. They use something like a million litres a year, quite a large figure, and they are doing really impressive things but also seeing the economic gains in doing that as well, with electrification of everything from trucks to diggers to all the smaller vehicles they have.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Numerous reports show Australia is the biggest importer of diesel and the biggest consumer of diesel per capita in the world. What are we going to do to shake our exposure to this imported fossil fuel that is driving inflation across the country?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Coming back to some comments made earlier to Senator Pocock, within the context of the legislated net zero commitment and its interim targets, there are a range of different policies that have different effects. We have talked briefly about the safeguard. That does provide an economic incentive for companies to decarbonise. They will do that where they can see, in most cases, the most cost-effective way of doing that. In some cases, that's through diesel efficiency measures or switching to alternative fuels or processes. Mr Edwards has talked about electrification at some mine sites, for example. Below safeguard facilities, different policies apply. We talked briefly earlier in the day about the new vehicle efficiency standard, which is providing Australians with greater options for efficient vehicles. You will see some switching from motorists previously driving diesel vehicles to more efficient or different, say, electrified vehicles. There's also work underway with the government's, I believe, $1.1 billion commitment to a low-carbon liquid fuel demand-side measure.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Sorry to interrupt. Is there anyone apart from Fortescue reducing diesel use?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: There's a range, but, again, they don't generally report to us exactly how they've achieved their emissions targets; they just acquit to the Clean Energy Regulator. We would certainly have other case studies where people—
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Would you mind providing those on notice?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, I am happy to see what we can give you.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, if we can provide top-line case studies. I think the safeguard mechanism is expected to deliver a reduction in diesel use of about 18 billion litres by 2035. You're right to say that Australia is—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm just addressing that figure—thank you, Minister—versus how many offsets they're using, just to clarify.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes. The way that the mechanism works, of course, is that firms go to the lowest-cost reductions that they can first. The further you go into the operation of the scheme, the more likely is that harder-to-abate questions like diesel use become the subject of practical action. So it is 18 billion litres by 2035. There are measures like $70 million in financing for Volvo to accelerate electrification of trucks. Every 100,000 electric vehicle sales take about three days off national petrol consumption every year.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Minister, I know that, but I'm about to run out of time.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: So each of the practical measures that—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

text: Senator Hodgins-May, I'll come back to you once we've given a block to the coalition. Senator Henderson.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you, Minister. Thanks for that.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: And I will continue to remind you, Minister, that none of these 27 projects are guaranteed to go ahead. They've all been withdrawn from this scheme. I will just go back to Ms Wiltshire, please.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Some were. As I outlined earlier, there were various different reasons why they withdrew. As I think my colleagues have outlined, the landscape's changed and some bid too low, and they have bid into our subsequent tenders. There were other projects that ultimately weren't able to get access to the network. Some were in a situation where they had received a power purchase agreement or an offer for a power purchase agreement, and that had been withdrawn, so their projects weren't viable in that regard. They need to find a new PPA. Some had delays to things like environmental approvals. Others had just broader changes in project circumstances. In some cases, projects had changed ownership, so those companies may not have wished to proceed. So they're quite varied.

text: Thank you. I want to just quickly go to the Cheaper Home Batteries Program because I just want to clarify something: It was confirmed this morning that, between 1 July 2025 and 27 September 2026, $4.63 billion was expended on the Cheaper Home Batteries Program. Given there was a budgeted amount in the 2025-26 budget, could you please just take me through what was budgeted and what was actually expended in the financial year 2025-26.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: In the financial year 2025-26, $3.95 billion was expended.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
witness_position: Branch Head, Renewable Certificates Scheme Branch

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Was that the budgeted amount or was that the actual spend?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
witness_position: Branch Head, Renewable Certificates Scheme Branch

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
witness_position: Branch Head, Renewable Certificates Scheme Branch

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
witness_position: Branch Head, Renewable Certificates Scheme Branch

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What do you mean by 'the original project settings'?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
witness_position: Branch Head, Renewable Certificates Scheme Branch

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

text: When I have a look at the budget and the forwards, I see that around half of the $8.5 billion has been expended already. What is going to change? I know Senator Smith was drilling into this previously, but it's unclear as to how the department and the minister are going to rein in this program to meet the forward estimates projections, which are dramatically below what has been spent to date.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The rate of expenditure has fallen, and, as I said, the 1 May changes, on average, reduced subsidy rates by about 50 per cent. There are now six-monthly step-downs in the level of the discount going forward, so that is going to lead to a reduction in expenditures.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
witness_position: Branch Head, Renewable Certificates Scheme Branch

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Do you have any modelling to support that? When I look at what's forecast in the budget—if I look at the forward estimates—I see that you've got, for 2025-26, $3.4 billion—we know now that it was $3.9 billion in actual expenditure—for 2026-27 it's $1.46 billion, for 2027-28 it's $1.2 billion, for 2028-29 it's $1.1 billion and for 2029-30 it's $906 million. These are dramatic changes in the program. What modelling do you have to support the view that the changes in design will allow you to achieve what has been projected in the forward estimates?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Modelling was undertaken at the time that the government adjusted the program last year.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Modelling was undertaken this time last year to support those changes that were put into place, and the government has undertaken to continue to monitor the take-up of the program.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
witness_position: Branch Head, Renewable Certificates Scheme Branch

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
witness_position: Branch Head, Renewable Certificates Scheme Branch

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: My question, though, is: does the modelling show that you will be able to achieve what's in the forward estimates, which, as I say, is a dramatic change from $3.9 billion expended in the last financial year down to $1.2 billion in 2027-28 and $1.1 billion in 2028-29?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, I think what it means is that two million Australians are now going to get access to a home battery.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Minister, if Mr Johnson could just be permitted to answer the question—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm entitled to jump in. Two million Australians will get access to a home battery. That means they will have lower electricity bills, and it will be good for the electricity network. It is a very popular scheme.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Minister, this is an example of gross economic incompetence in terms of how this project has been managed. It was initially $2.3 billion and has blown out to $8.5 billion.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Lower electricity bills—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You're spending money like drunken sailors, Minister.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, there will be lower electricity bills for households and lower costs for Australians. Gas-fired generation during the evening peak averaged 1,385 megawatts, down 50 per cent year on year. That means lower bills for Australians and lower wholesale electricity costs. Batteries supplied more electricity than gas during the evening peak all the way through a whole quarter, and thousands of Australians, two million, ultimately—I mean, the seat of Hume, Mr Taylor's seat, has the sixth-biggest take-up. These are not Australians in inner cities who are picking this up, largely. This is outer suburban—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Minister, electricity prices are going through the roof. Gas is up by more than 40 per cent.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, for these households, two million households, their costs are much lower, and they're contributing to lower wholesale costs for the whole system. If you think that's bad economic management, that explains a lot of things.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think it is appalling economic management—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It is a roaring success.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: that a program costed at $2.3 billion could blow out to $8.5 billion. It is so poorly designed. It is gross mismanagement by you and your government.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It is a roaring success. It is working for ordinary households.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It is a disaster, Minister.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I understand—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It is a shocking embarrassment, which is one of the reasons that Australians are losing faith in your government.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: In mainstream Australia, this is delivering lower costs for businesses. There are 6,890 or so households in the seat of Hume—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Chris Bowen should not have this job. He is so incompetent—

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Let's just focus on that part of outer suburban and regional Australia.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senators, could we just come to order for one moment, please.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Three million-plus dollars of public funds on a potentially dud project is concerning.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: They will be managing those questions. In terms of carbon capture and storage, I'm interested in developments in the sector, but I'm not sure whether this particular event tells us very much about it at all.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Are you confident we'll get those funds back?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The Business Grants Hub will pursue to the extent they can, but again, my understanding is that proponent is in administration, so they would need to work through that process with other creditors.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Just staying on CCA—I know I've only got a minute or two left—at the gas tax inquiry, we heard significant evidence about the long-term costs to taxpayers of decommissioning and rehabilitation of offshore oil and gas projects. The 2026-27 budget papers include an unquantifiable contingent liability relating to the Gorgon CCS project, including an indemnity to the Western Australian government. Are you able to shed some light on why the Commonwealth liability is still classified as unquantifiable?

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think the liability of existing oil and gas projects—those sort of questions should go to the Department of Industry, Science and Resources.
witness_organisation: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Okay. Perhaps if you would like to take it on notice as well, in case there is anything, but I will also take the questioning to them. Thank you.

agency: Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That will conclude outcome 1, so thank you very much to the officials who have contributed and given evidence in that respect. I'm just going to ask broadcasting to suspend for one moment, please, while I have a very quick conversation with my colleagues on the committee, and then we will move to our next stage.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We now welcome officers from the Clean Energy Finance Corporation, including Mr Paul McCartney, the CEO. Mr McCartney, do you have an opening statement?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I do.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: If you would like to make a short opening statement and then table it after that, that would be wonderful.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
Thank you very much. I thank the committee for the opportunity to provide a short opening statement. I'm the new Chief Executive Officer for the CEFC. This is my first appearance. I've been with the CEFC for over 13 years and was most recently the CIO for the $19 billion Rewiring the Nation program to help modernise our grid. Over that time, I oversaw over $10 billion of commitments under that fund. I also want to recognise my predecessor, Ian Learmonth, who led the CEFC through a stage of remarkable growth and development. This is an incredibly important time as we lay the foundations for our energy future. I view the energy transition underway not just as an emissions story but also as being about the important reforms and economic advantages of adopting more modern and productive technologies to help ensure Australia's future energy competitiveness and resilience. Having worked at the CEFC for as long as I have, I can state we've built an extraordinary team of professionals, delivering on behalf of the Australian Government and the Australian people, of which I'm very proud. I'm determined to ensure CEFC continues to think ahead of the curve and be ready and responsive.

I'd just like to highlight three achievements in our annual report that was published just last week. Last year, we had a record $9.1 billion in investment commitments with a total project value of $19.6 billion. Our investments are creating real benefits for Australians. An example is the concessional finance program for Marinus Link, which is expected to deliver $900 million in savings to Tasmanian and Victorian energy consumers, reducing the impact of transmission related costs by about 45 per cent than what they would have otherwise been. Our lifetime commitments for CEFC are now a bit over $27 billion, and we have delivered over $104 billion in project value for Australians. Thank you for your time, and I welcome questions from the committee.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you very much, Mr McCartney. I go to Senator Henderson.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
Good afternoon, and welcome to your first estimates. I want to ask you about the quotes you gave the industry publication Renew Economy on 16 October. You said:

Hyperinflation had added costs to wind farm projects.

Can you qualify what hyperinflation has added either in dollar or percentage terms to the cost of wind projects overall?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The approximate numbers that we're seeing are an increase in, if you like, the PPA value required to get wind farms up, and that varies between about a 20 and 30 per cent number over the last two or three years.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Between 20 and 30 per cent higher overall?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Over the last two to three years, correct.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: And what's driven that very substantial increase in costs?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think that's the general inflation around the world today. So these projects, all major projects we're seeing across the country, are now suffering increasing costs over time. So going back to—there was a post-COVID reaction where inflation spiked, and then the wars have also exacerbated that. So it's a global phenomenon where we're seeing increased cost on large-scale projects but projects of this nature.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: If you're able to provide us with the details of this hyperinflation number on notice, we would be grateful, so we can understand how you have reached that particular conclusion.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Some of the data that I'm sharing is commercial-in-confidence. These are observations directly from wind farms as we try to negotiate with them on financing arrangements to get them to close. We will do our best to provide that.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, please, if you could, provide as much information in relation to the wind farm projects that you are dealing with. I guess my concern is that perhaps the CEFC is laying the groundwork to justify investing more money, more and more taxpayers' money essentially, in wind farm projects. Is that the case?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Our role under our act is to invest into renewable energy and help creating the private sector finance to support those projects. I think it's fair to say we've seen a hiatus in wind farm delivery over the last few years, and the ISP and AEMO's advice is that we do require wind as part of our energy mix. So under our act and guidance, we will be trying to help those wind farm projects close in a timely manner.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: How are you going to be trying to help them? What's your plan?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: With our financing—some of the pressures they are facing are an absolute return pressure on the wind farms. We have the ability to provide concessional finance. Some of the other pressures we're seeing at the moment are a bit of a withdrawal of the Australian banks from the renewable sector or less appetite. So there is a liquidity issue facing the sector itself where there's enough financing available to get these projects to closure.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Could you please describe the negotiations that you're currently undertaking with various projects in relation to finance and what you might be considering providing.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I can't share commercial-in-confidence information. What I can share is we have a number of large-scale renewable projects we're currently negotiating with. We've been negotiating with them for some time, and we're looking to support them this year.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Which wind farm projects are they?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I cannot name that.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Can anyone else name them, or can you bring that information to the table?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We usually don't talk about projects that are under negotiation with our counterparts. It would be a breach of our confidentiality obligation with those counterparts.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, that's not a reason not to answer the question, Mr McCartney—just because it's confidential. This is Senate estimates, so I am seeking that information.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think the official will take that on notice.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That's fine.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: And we'll consider our approach to that. I understand the objection that you raise. However, it is a material question about the Commonwealth's financial position in these and undermining the Commonwealth's financial position in negotiations. But I understand that territory we traverse there, which is why I say we'll just take that question on notice.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It's also a competitive market. So we wouldn't want to be divulging some without having—

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: But, Mr Every, we've just heard that the competitive markets have collapsed. The banks are withdrawing. Wind farm projects are not being financed. So I don't know that's an appropriate—

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The market's still competitive even for our finance, as in there are a number of transactions around Australia that are all looking for support, and the nature of banking is that you can't really divulge commercial negotiations about one counterpart and where you're up to without disturbing the markets for others.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, that particular question has been taken on notice, Mr Every.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That's correct, yes.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: But I do remind you that you are at Senate estimates. There are very important accountability purposes for the role that estimates plays. This is a very important role of the parliament. Can I please ask—

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You've asked quite a narrow question, which is for a list. We'll consider that and come back to you on notice.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you, Minister. Can I ask: what's the overall quantum of underwriting support that is being sought from the CEFC?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: By the wind farms?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That's right.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: There wouldn't be a precise number on that at the moment. We do have a forward pipeline that is significant.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: And what is the overall quantum in terms of dollars for that pipeline?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, that pipeline could be up to in the order of over a billion dollars, but that's in negotiation.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Okay. So over a billion dollars of potential funding is under negotiation. Can you be more precise than 'over a billion'? It's not several billion or $10 billion. It's over—

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It's not several billion.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It's over $1 billion, though. And how many projects are we talking about?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I would have to take that on notice and come back to you.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Are we talking three or four, 10, 20? Just a ballpark?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Ballpark would be less than 10.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Will this additional funding require additional appropriations from the government? Do you have this money lying around, or would you be seeking for further government contribution?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I wouldn't describe it as 'we have this money lying around'.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, I'm being a little bit flippant with the way I say that, but would you be seeking a further government appropriation?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Not for our immediate pipeline that we have currently, no.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: So is this funding, the over the $1 billion, being contemplated being expended in this financial year or committed in this financial year?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: These are very large complex projects, so, while our target may be to try and achieve commitment on these projects issue, they can take longer. I would say if we were to commit this financial year by 30 June 2027, the drawing down of those projects would take a number of years.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The fact that there has been this shortfall in private investment—doesn't it concern you that there is very significant evidence that these projects are no longer commercially viable?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I guess that's an easy inference to draw, but what I might explain is, when we look at these projects, that we ensure that they have appropriate contracting and that they're able to service the debt that we are looking to provide, along with the other commercial debt that's available. What I'd say is, in our pipeline, we will, by no means, be the sole funder. There will be an appropriate level of equity provided typically by large institutional investors and energy providers here domestically as well as internationally. That will be first in line for any risk, and we will be pari passu in terms of the commercial banking sector, which is what we typically are in these projects. What I would describe is that there may be an absolute return issue with the projects themselves—CEFC concessional finance may help bridge some of that—or there may just be a shortfall in liquidity. These are significant projects for the Australian market, requiring deep pools of capital.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
Can I just ask you about the quote from you, saying:

What we saw with Tomago is potentially an opportunity there to get PPAs written to help drag the wind through and unblock things.

Can I confirm that from this comment that the CEFC is looking to undertake more Tomago-style underwriting?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, I think the point of that quote was that CEFC is looking to still fund renewables in a market that has become more difficult for renewables, and, in an instance where you have large industrial demand such as Tomago, or it could be data centres, providing the PPAs, that's an opportunity to pull through those renewables projects into the sector and have CEFC bank them and bank them in a way that is secure so that we're not losing or risking finance on behalf of Australian taxpayers.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I've just got a range of other questions. I'm just going to move through before I ask for Senator Smith to be given the call. I want to understand, with the Rewiring the Nation Fund, what's been expended to date, and how much has been contractually committed?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'll answer this quite carefully, if that's okay. When we commit to projects, we have a contractual obligation to fund those to a particular amount. Our commitment to date under the Rewiring the Nation Fund is $10.6 billion.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: And what is under negotiation? How much is under negotiation? The fund is worth some, what, $20 billion?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Our current fund is worth $19.65 billion.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Pretty close to $20 billion.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Pretty close to $20 billion, true.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Alright. Thank you.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We have a number of other projects currently under negotiation which would take us close to that number of $19.65 billion. I think you asked another question before about the total deployed in Rewiring the Nation. We've deployed a total, out of the $10.6 billion, of a bit over $2 billion. As at 30 June, we've had some repayments of those funds that were deployed, so we're down to about $1.6 billion in deployed funds. That reflects the nature of these very large projects. Marinus Link is an example. Our commitment there is $3.8 billion, and that will probably start drawing in December of this year.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I want to ask about the investment mandate. It requires the Rewiring the Nation Fund to have a rate of return of 1.00 as a ratio of direct costs. What is the current actual rate of return?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think it's slightly below that. I'd have to look that up, or Simon might be able to find that.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We'll get that for you—just a second.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think what that would reflect is we're in the early stage of the fund where the numbers I just shared—out of the $10.6 billion, only about $1.7 billion is deployed. That's what's out there earning interest. We've got a line of sight on that improving and achieving that 1.00 target.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Why are you running under the benchmark rate of return? And I'm still waiting to get that number.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It's the way it's calculated. It's a calculation of our costs versus our interest income and fees received. While we haven't deployed all of our money, we don't achieve—we don't typically receive interest income on money that's committed but not yet deployed. As we deploy that full $10.6 billion, we will start earning interest on the money that's deployed—our borrowers will start paying us—and that number will come up above that one.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What is your latest annualised return?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Generally for CEFC or—

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
