agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We measure that on the disclosure that you just asked about, which is the—

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Apologies, I've jumped back. I'm still waiting to get the—

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm just trying to get that for you. Sorry.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: actual rate of return for the RTN Fund. While we wait for that number, do you have the annualised return numbers?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: For the Rewiring the Nation Fund?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I can answer that if you don't mind bearing with me for a moment.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: While Paul is getting that number, you asked about the general portfolio rate of return?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That's 4.28 per cent.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. Also, what is the latest retained surplus accumulated losses for the RTN?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Just for the RTN?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, please.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Okay.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I might share the call with Senator Pocock and then come back.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Alright. Can I just get an answer to that and also how much funding is sitting in the RTN special account. And, sorry, to finish these questions, the Prime Minister announced CEFC would set aside a $3 billion investment through RTN for Western Australia. I'm keen to know how much of that $3 billion has been expended to date.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No funds have been committed to date with Western Australia. We are in active discussions with Western Australia about a number of projects, both in their south-west interconnected system and in the Pilbara north-west system.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Why has there been no funding committed?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, sorry, why have there been no—

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation

text: Commitments.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: commitments that have flowed from that funding?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: For some time now, we've been working with the Western Australian government around the Pilbara—around some particular projects up there. They have a plan for the Pilbara. I understand that that's currently under consideration by the Western Australian government. As those projects get defined and we can assess them in terms of our financing, we'll take appropriate decisions at that point.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Alright. Anything further, could we have on notice on the WA negotiations. If you could, detail what projects are under negotiation.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We can't share the negotiations, but we could share what's in the public domain about the projects that are under contemplation.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, I am asking for details about what's under negotiation, please.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'd have to take that on notice. Going back to where we had that other conversation, there's risk that we can expose the Commonwealth and taxpayers.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Going back to the RTN special account, do you have how much is sitting in the special account?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I don't think we've got a breakdown of how much is sitting in the special account because that's administered by the department and our commitments don't draw until we need them. How it works is we've got the credits sitting to our name in the special account, and then, when we've got a project that has been financed, we exercise a draw notice, provide the minister and department with details necessary for that, and then the department would provide the cash necessary for us to fulfil those stages. For example, on Marinus Link, we wouldn't necessarily draw the full commitment on day one.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Alright. Could I ask for that further information on notice. I've got to finish up my block.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Along with the retained surplus accumulated losses for the RTN.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation

text: Will do.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Pocock.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you for your time this afternoon. In April, the AFR reported that the CEFC was negotiating several deals involving data centres. Have any of those been finalised yet?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: None have been finalised as yet. We're in the final stages of a term sheet which will go to formal contractual documents, not with a greenfield data centre but with an existing one. We've been under those negotiations for a considerable amount of time. Measure that in years, not months. It's a small data centre, and I think it's likely that that's probably the only data centre that I can see we would have a direct involvement with in a funding sense. That was done—entered into—around the time of the report that I think was mentioned earlier that CEFC participated in. I guess what we'll get out of that is learnings around green energy for data centres and how viable that is—also recycled waters and things like that. It's not a significant investment in terms of what the CEFC does. I think also in that report there was mention of a data centre pipeline for the CEFC. I think the way that we view data centres today is a bit like our industrial users of energy. We see our role of creating as much renewable energy as we can not only to service data centres and industrials but also for the benefit of consumers more generally.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Okay. I have couple of questions from that. If it's a small data centre and a fairly small deal, why has it taken years of the CEFC's time?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: These things just take time. It's really up to the speed of what the project proponent works at. We commenced discussions with that proponent, from memory, back in early '25, and now they're at a stage where it's coming live. So we could conclude that in the near future.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Is that an Australian-owned company?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It's a global investor with local operations in data centres.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Is there no delineation within the CEFC in terms of financing sovereign, Australian companies versus—why would the CEFC be giving a global company a leg-up with data centres when it seems like there are hundreds of billions of dollars being thrown at data centres by the big end of town?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Look, I probably agree with your last statement, and that's why we don't have a pipeline that we're actively pursuing in data centres. Our involvement in this project is to drive them to acquire green energy and other ESG initiatives within the project. Otherwise, they simply would not do it. That's what our participation is about. It's an emerging and a new sector, so I think us getting to know and understand, from the inside, those sectors is important. In terms of global investors, we actually see it as critical to Australia that we do encourage global investors to come and invest here across all of our infrastructure—energy and everything else. The quantum of the investment that's required through to 2050 is significant, so the extent to which we can help encourage that is something that we're always trying to do.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: To add, our legislation contains a provision that requires that all of our investments be solely or mainly Australian based, and that keeps us focused on the Australian market. If you look across the energy system and many other sectors of the economy, there's a large participation by foreign investors in the Australian market. As a part of having influence and getting the sectoral change that we need to do to decarbonise Australia, we work with those foreign investors into Australia and even try to bring new foreign investment into the country where it will help facilitate our objectives, which are given to us by the government and the parliament. There are also some requirements for us to participate in Australian industry participation plans for large project financings, and we would work with the Australian industry department as part of government to put those requirements on developers and so forth.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Mr McCartney, how are you driving the project towards using renewable energy?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We've got contractual obligations under our financing arrangements that they have to deliver it.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: This is obviously being done before the national expectations for data centres come into effect.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: So there's no obligation around renewables?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: There's an obligation to acquire renewable energy, a hundred per cent, to run their facility, bearing in mind this has been getting negotiated since, I think, August 2025, by memory.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That would be an obligation that we're requesting of the counterpart, because this was small and predates the government's—

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Also, this data centre is under the scale, I think, of the intended requirements under legislation from the government.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Can you say what those obligations are without compromising any sort of commercial-in-confidence negotiations?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not sure that they've been finalised yet.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I might prefer to get that accurate and take it on notice, if that's okay.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Okay. Is there another mechanism to finance data centres, or this is kind of a one-off and you don't—this is not the next?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We don't see this as a long-term investment strategy for CEFC, investing into data centres. I think, as you commented, they appear to be very well funded and they appear to be getting significant capital globally, so I don't think that's a role for us. Our bigger concern, strategically, is on the energy system for Australia—not just for data centres but for all consumers, and, going back to where we started, trying to drive through some of those renewables into the system with our support.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. Finally, you've said, Mr Every, solely or mainly Australia based.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What does that mean in practice? Does it have a component of retained economic benefit or can it just be a multinational that is building something here?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It's a holistic test. Under the act, the board is actually empowered to set guidelines as to what 'solely or mainly Australian based' means. Those guidelines are published on the CEFC's website. In practical terms, we're looking for projects which will either take out a large piece of abatement or establish a new technology class or establish a credit precedent. So we're not looking to finance any project. When it comes to the solely or mainly Australian based test, what we're really trying to see there is the level of commitment of this business to Australia, what this particular investment is going to do, how it is replicable in this market, how it demonstrates to other Australian businesses that this is a pathway forward that can be followed if it is a genuinely fresh entry into the market.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. Thanks, Chair.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you, Senator Pocock. Senator Henderson.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. Look, I just wanted to ask about CEFC's investment in equity in Tasmania Natural Asset Trust. That was approved on 12 August 2025, and this relates to the acquisition of Rushy Lagoon. At the time you approved that investment, had DAFF completed its plantation forestry agricultural impact assessment?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: On 12 August?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, at the time you approved the investment.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The time of investment approval was 12 August 2025. I would have to take on notice the actual status of the particular completion of that requirement that you've specified, but it's not unusual for us to move a transaction through the investment process subject to the conclusion of legal and other requirements that we need.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: CEFC has said that its investment was not conditional on FIRB approval, ACCU registration, plantation establishment or Commonwealth grant funding. Is that correct?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I might clarify that. We weren't subject under Commonwealth grant funding that was ultimately received; that was received after we had closed that transaction. In respect of FIRB, it's not unusual for us to take an equity investment with an international party that requires FIRB. However, the project and our funding can't conclude until FIRB gives its appropriate approval for the transaction. The parties won't come and approach FIRB unless they have certainty that they have a real project there to proceed with. So it's not unusual for us to invest or commit to a project that requires FIRB approval as a conditions precedent before we fund the project and finally commit contractually. So that project, we had a commitment with the investment partners Gresham and Aviva. They then went and sought their appropriate FIRB approval, we wait until FIRB approval had occurred, otherwise the funding approach itself could not conclude.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: So what material did you rely on to make the investment decision that you did, and to satisfy yourself about agricultural land use conversion, the plantation establishment, ACCU participation and also FIRB approval? I accept that it wasn't at that point granted, but you made an investment decision. What did you rely on to make that investment decision?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We do very detailed analysis of projects of that nature. So we did a detailed assessment of the manager, a detailed assessment of our investment partners. We looked at the project itself and what was involved in it and satisfied ourselves that there is in fact a viable project there that could be concluded, and off the back of the ACCUs. Now, we have a number of projects where we've taken a future assessment of what the ACCU market will look like, and we do that with the assistance of renowned or well-qualified modellers and forecasters in those markets. So we looked at that in the same way we would look at any other investment that we undertake. The project itself, of course, couldn't conclude until FIRB had given their approval.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: This is a very controversial project which has caused enormous grief, particularly in Tasmania. Your own investment paper says the social risk associated with converting agricultural land to plantation forestry was assessed as low. Who made that assessment? This has been horrendous for the people of Tasmania. This is precious farmland that has been lost.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
There is a paper that we will table. You're probably aware that there is a Tasmanian government inquiry. We will be appearing at that inquiry at the appropriate time. We've made a submission that is public, but for the benefit of the Senate we will table that today as well, in hard copies. I would refer to that submission, which I said is public. On the last page there is a copy of the Tasmanian government's assessment of that farming land as degraded. That was not our assessment; it's the Tasmanian government's assessment.

So when we looked at that, we looked at what is the highest and best use of the land—this is detailed in our submission—and found that for agricultural purposes, as it was, with the three dairying operations, one of which had ceased operations, were not viable. In fact, through the process we tried, or our partners tried, to acquire the land absent the dairying operations, and the deceased estate of the vendor, who was an international investor, would not separate the dairying operations. The reason we or our investor partners looked to separate it was to make this an investment that's viable. What was found is the dairying operations were that dilapidated that the capex cost to restore it and make them functional wouldn't provide sufficient return for an investor. Post that, we've tried, or our investment partners tried, to sell the dairying operations, as it were, to separate it from the land so they could continue. There have been no bidders or buyers for those dairying operations in Tasmania.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I might just clarify two items there.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: So you're going to table that?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, we will table that.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Could you do that now? Is that possible?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Sure.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: As soon as you can facilitate that. As I say, this is an investment to a foreign entity that has—because a lot of Tasmanians take a very different view. They consider this land to be very precious—

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
Well, that's because they've been told by you and your colleagues that this is prime agricultural land, and it simply isn't. The dairy asset is unable to be sold. This is a foreign owned agricultural mixed-use facility that was sold to another owner. Tasmania's own classification system, in a system that goes from prime agricultural land 1 through to the bottom, classifies this as 5, 6 and 7, depending on which parcel of land you're talking about. If it's to sell, the dairy part of the operation failed. No credible buyer could be found.

But it's also not true to say that this land won't be used in part for farming. There's 3,000 head of cattle currently grazing, supporting six jobs. There will be cropping as part of the property's ongoing use. It will produce around five million tonnes of construction-grade timber, which will be available for processing in Tasmanian saw mills and will support the construction of Australian homes. The overall project will support 190 jobs: planting, forestry, grazing and restoration work. It was already entirely foreign owned. It's now 49 per cent Australian owned. No native vegetation is going to be cleared for plantations. The way that this has been represented is completely inconsistent with the facts.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, I'm asking the questions, Minister, and so I am raising—

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not complaining about the questions; I'm complaining about the representations.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I am raising legitimate concerns about this investment and the due diligence undertaken by the CEFC. So the chair of the CEFC sits on the board of FIRB; that's correct?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Steven is currently on the board or a member of FIRB; I'm not sure of that categorisation.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: In terms of the decision by FIRB, what steps were taken to manage that particular situation where there could be a potential conflict of interest?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I can't answer the steps that FIRB took. I can answer—

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, I'm asking about the CEFC's steps.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Sure. Within the CEFC this project was under our delegated approvals, which means it's a decision for our internal management investment committee, comprised of our executive, who approved the project. So it didn't actually go to the board for approval per se. It did go to the board to keep them informed on the way through. Steven, the chair of CEFC, who has the potential conflict mentioned, was recused in all circumstances and discussions on this project.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: So he sat on the FIRB board, but he recused himself in relation to any investment decisions by the CEFC. Is that correct?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: He was not involved in any process of investment decision around the decision to invest in Rushy Lagoon at CEFC. If I may, I just want to clarify something I said before about reference to the land as being degraded. I just want to correctly read that for the record. The Rushy Lagoon is marginal land consisting of classes 5, 6 and 7. This is under the Tasmanian government's classification system. Class 5 is non-arable land suitable for pastoral use and grazing, requiring groundcover management to prevent erosion. Class 6 is low-intensity grazing land with severe physical or climactic limitations. Class 7 is land with very severe to extreme limitations which make it unsuitable for agricultural use. So just for the record, I want to be clear that's how that land has been designated.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Less than 14 per cent of the property has historically been allocated to dairy farming. Less than 14 per cent. And that part of it couldn't be separated and sold because nobody would buy it—

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm just trying to quickly—

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: because it was so degraded.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I just want to go back to this conflict-of-interest issue. Mr Skala recused himself from the investment decisions. Was there any probity certificate in relation to the potential conflict of interest?

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm trying to think how I answer that question best. I think the best way to answer it is when any of our board potentially have conflict that has arisen, at the time that the conflict arises—Steven's participation in FIRB was noted to our board. I can't tell you the specific date, but probably when he joined FIRB. So we were aware that any projects coming up that do require the purvey of FIRB under our board, Steven would be recused from, in that sense, and not privy to any of that information.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The procedures that are required to be followed are set under the PGPA Act rules, and we follow those rigorously inside the CEFC. We also establish information barriers where somebody is at risk of potential conflict. We ensure that investment papers, for example, are not distributed to the individual who is recused from attending the meeting. There's a detailed register of the declarations of interest made by people, and that's required under the PGPA Act as well. Then, as the conflicts are noted or registered, we put in place a set of procedures to ensure that rigorous compliance with the integrity legislation is in place at all times.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Alright. We've got a range of other questions that we will put on notice due to time, but thank you very much for your time.

agency: Clean Energy Finance Corporation
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you very much. On that note, we will suspend for 10 minutes for afternoon tea, and at that point I will welcome officers from Snowy Hydro Ltd. For now, thank you very much to the officers from the Clean Energy Finance Corporation for their evidence and the work that goes into preparing for these hearings.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We now call officers from Snowy Hydro Ltd. Welcome, and I welcome Mr Dennis Barnes, the chief executive officer. If you'd like to, give an opening statement, and then I'll turn to questions.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
Thank you for the opportunity today. I'd like to acknowledge the Ngunnawal people, on whose land we are meeting. We have released the outcome of the cost reassessment for Snowy 2.0, which sets a target cost of $22.2 billion and a cost scenario of $25 billion. I understand this is extremely disappointing. I share that disappointment. Snowy 2.0 is an immensely complex project. There are more than 5,000 people working directly on the project. They are working hard and efficiently and making progress. Amongst other things, it was underestimated how many people were needed and for how long. Snowy 2.0 costs are 80 per cent people related.

In 2023, Snowy 2.0 was effectively stalled. Local suppliers weren't being paid, and $4 billion of contractor claims sat on the table. This was recognised by the previous management, and a cash flow support agreement was in place to support our contractor. The original fixed price contract for Snowy 2.0 had failed. It was not the right type of contract for this project's unique scale and complexity and the resultant risk. This list of claims was growing, inflamed by the unproductive and adversarial relationship between Snowy Hydro and our contractor. We would be in a worse position today if we did not reset the contract.

At the reset, we moved to a more conventional contract type—an incentivised target cost model, or ITC. At the reset, the contractor received zero margin for their work to that point. That reset gives Snowy open-book visibility on risk and cost, which prompted the cost reassessment. Under a fixed-price contract, we would not have had the visibility to know we had a problem nor the ability to take corrective action.

The new contract has been characterised as a cost-plus contract. This is not an accurate way to describe the contract, which is a very common contract for complex mega projects in Australia, for good reason. ITC contracts incentivises efficient delivery. Our contractor stands to make more money if the delivery and efficiency targets are exceeded and, conversely, be penalised if not. But it also allows unexpected additional costs to be accommodated so that delivery progress can continue, only when they are verified and agreed upon by both parties as well as by our independent cost auditors. Under the ITC model, productivity doubled within 12 months. We are discussing a very disappointing cost increase but in the context of a project that is making progress. We are 95 per cent of the way through the drill-and-blast tunnels; that figure was around 15 per cent at the reset. We are 65 per cent of the way through the tunnel-boring machine tunnels; we were 19 per cent at the reset. We are 90 per cent of the way through excavation of the power station caverns, large enough to fit the Sydney Opera House, and we were effectively at zero per cent at reset.

Snowy 2.0 will be a national asset designed to operate for 150 years, providing more than half of the grid's storage. In addition to the returns Snowy Hydro will make on Snowy 2.0 and the enabling of 67,000 megawatts of renewables, it will underpin reliability, lower wholesale prices by $7 billion in the first few decades, and contribute more than $18 billion to the economy through construction. We've largely overcome the design immaturity at the final investment decision that is the root cause for most of the project's cost increases. At the point of the reset, only 44 per cent of the construction design was complete. Today, that figure is 96 per cent complete. In a project of this nature, there will always be risk. However, we are now much further progressed than we were, and the risk exposure is reducing. Thank you again for the opportunity to meet today, and I welcome your questions.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you, Mr Barnes. I actually have a couple of questions to lead off before I go to Senator Roberts. Picking up on where you finished just then, can I just ask: was the initial $2 billion headline cost of Snowy 2.0 ever feasible?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No decisions were ever made on the $2 billion headline figure. Clearly, events to date show that it was an infeasible figure.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: A big difference between $2 billion and $25 billion, Chair—come on.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, I agree. That initial $2 billion was absurd.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Seriously, the blowout. It was $6 billion in 2022.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: But, Senator Henderson, please don't interrupt me while I am asking my questions.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, Chair, I just want to put the facts on the record.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: And you will have your chance to do that, but we don't interrupt you while you are asking your questions, so please leave it.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It was over $6 billion in 2022.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson!

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Now it's $25 billion.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson, come to order! Can I just ask you, Mr Barnes: how has the design immaturity at financial investment decision impacted the project? You touched upon that at the end there. If you are able to, can you elaborate on that a bit, please.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: If we go to the reset target cost, which was $12 billion, and today let's choose the $22 billion figure that the contractor has provided, that's a $10 billion difference, and about three-quarters is as a result of design immaturity, $5 billion is associated with more people for longer, a little over $1 billion on scope that was omitted because of the poor design and about $1 billion on specific design elements that were missed. The balance of about $2½ billion is associated with the escalation factors we've seen across all projects.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. Senator Roberts.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you, Mr Barnes, and your staff, for being here again. When will the money borrowed to pay for this project, including bonds, be paid off? What year?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We finance Snowy 2.0 at the company level, so at Snowy Hydro level. Private debt and our shareholder loans, so loans from the government, have a range of debt repayment profiles. I think for the shareholder loan there's a soon-as-reasonably-practical obligation. You've used the word 'bonds'. We don't want to specifically use bonds, but I presume you mean in bank debt and shareholder debt.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, I do. So what year?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: it will be paid off progressively.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: So what year will it be finished paying off?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We will always hold a debt balance as Snowy Hydro. So we will never go to zero debt.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: When will you pay off 95 per cent?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We will never go to zero bonds. We will always hold—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, that's leaving a five per cent balance. So when will you go to 95 per cent paid?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I don't have a repayment profile in my head.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Could you take it on notice?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I don't think we would be able to model that, to be honest, but we're happy to take it on notice and see what we can provide. We could probably provide the debt roll-off profile that we will be required to repay or refinance.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Whatever you think is needed for good stewardship of taxpayer money.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, of course.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It's not valid to say consolidated revenue has contributed to the cost of Snowy 2.0 when your government is running debt and finance deficits out past 2050. Every cent going into Snowy 2.0 is debt. How much is the total cost of the project, including the interest paid on capital through to—the year you wouldn't mention, but—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The $12 billion target cost that was approved in 2023 was a $4 billion equity contribution.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That was under the first or second year of the Albanese government.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It was in 2024, I think, that it was approved, yes—wherever that is in the political cycle. There was an additional shareholder loan provided which will be required to be paid back in the 2030s. Obviously, we've provided this disappointing advice to the government of the higher cost, and they are considering how they may support us through that higher cost. In terms of capitalised interest, again, we finance the organisation at the company level rather than the project level. I think in a prior hearing, I referred to between $2 billion and $3 billion of capitalised interest over the life of the project.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Could you total that up on notice, please.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, of course.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. So you've confirmed the current sunk cost is around $12 billion?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes. As at the end of June, we were just under $12 billion.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: And how much more would be incurred if the project was terminated right now, today?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We've not done that analysis for public consumption because obviously we are—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Have you done the analysis at all?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We have done the analysis of what would we do if we were to change contractor, as has been reported in the press, but we have not done the analysis on what it would cost to terminate the project, given the importance of the project to the grid.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
Okay, we'll get back to that again. Robert Gottliebsen in the Australian says: 'Snowy Hydro 2.0 has destroyed voters' faith in mega renewable energy projects. It's a laughing stock.' That was in the Australian last week. He made the comment in his story about the cost blowout that:

Worse still, there is no certainty that the project will actually work.

What confidence level, Mr Barnes, do you have that the project will generate the 375,000 megawatt hours of power each year, and, more generally, is there anything in this report to support Robert's statement?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The project will absolutely work. It doesn't generate 375 megawatt hours a year; it acts as a storage facility. Our modelling shows that it will actually absorb 6,000 gigawatt hours of electricity and produce 5,000 gigawatt hours of electricity. So it will absolutely work.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: So that's the inefficiencies of—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, 20 per cent—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: So you get less power out of it than you put into it?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, that's as any battery. To say it produces 375,000 megawatt hours is not a characterisation of its role. Its role is to absorb excess renewables, store those for the time when the grid needs it the most, and it will absolutely do that.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
Okay. Well, we'll go into the details at a later date. I note in your release, you say:

Closure of the project would cost 5,000 jobs.

Those are construction jobs, correct, not permanent jobs?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That's correct.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Is there no other project in Australia that those construction workers could get to work on? For example, the Brisbane, Queensland, Australian Olympics? Housing is desperate for workers, really desperate because the government is bringing in unskilled people. There are dams to build and power stations to build. Have you done any work on how your workforce could transition away from Snowy 2.0?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Taxpayers are subsidising an employment scheme. That's basically what Snowy 2.0 is at the moment. With subsidies, productivity decreases. We're decreasing the wealth of Australia. You can employ them on projects that will actually increase productivity of Australia. That would be wonderful for improving people's cost of living; it would be wonderful for higher pay rises that will be noninflationary. But, instead, you're doing the reverse: You're decreasing productivity when you could be refarming these people out, releasing them and getting on with higher productivity projects for the benefit of the country.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think from the government's perspective this is an important project that will strengthen energy security. You said earlier in a question today that you were worried about firming. This is a very important project in the context of the requirement for firming. As Mr Barnes said, the increasing costs is disappointing.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I reckon!

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: But it's a consequence of a decision by the previous government to—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I grant that we were criticising it back then.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: including your leader, Mr Joyce, to race to—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What's he leader of? I thought Pauline Hanson was the leader.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, I'll leave that to you guys. It was a race to a press release and, as Mr Joyce said, done on the back of a beer coaster. There are consequences when large infrastructure projects are run like that.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: There certainly are.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Increased costs are inevitable. Once you have a path dependency and poor engineering design, then the rectification costs for that, with the limited number of choices that you have—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: So you inherited that project. Why didn't you stop it right then in 2022?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Because it is an important project for the country.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: With the numbers involved as a load generation? Come on!

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Australians do hard things, and we are going to get through this project because it is required to make the country stronger.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: But most Australians do not do these kinds of things.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It is 65 per cent complete. We will see it through.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: For miniscule benefit. How much more is going to be lost?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
It is not a miniscule benefit. It is a very important national project. We will complete the project. There are consequences from a failure to do the design work by the Abbott, Turnbull and Morrison axis of disinvestment and disaster; that is true. Mr Joyce was a key architect of that, and Mr Taylor was the minister. Mr Taylor at the time said very encouraging things. He said, 'The economics stack up.' Mr Taylor said:

This is a great day for this region. This is a great day for Snowy Hydro. Most of all, this is a great day for Australia.

Senator Henderson interjecting—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, he was the one who bungled it.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
Senator Henderson.

Senator Henderson interjecting—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson!

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: $25 billion—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Come to order!

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
Mr Taylor—

Senator Henderson interjecting—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Sorry, Minister, just one second. Senator Henderson, you interrupted me, and now you have interrupted Senator Roberts. Please don't interrupt other senators when they're asking their questions.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not going to be bellowed over. Mr Taylor was the principal architect of this problem. He is the worst energy minister Australia—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You're the worst government—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: has ever had.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: we have ever had in this country.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
Senator Henderson, come to order!

Senator Henderson interjecting—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Nothing built.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson, come to order!

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
Cost blowouts, delay—

Senator Henderson interjecting—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
Disinvestment and decay.

Senator Henderson interjecting—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson!

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
That is Mr Taylor's legacy in energy terms.

Senator Henderson interjecting—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, no, Senator Henderson, he is making an observation about government, but he is answering a question from Senator Roberts. So will everyone please come to order. Minister, please finish your answer, and then we will go back to Senator Roberts for his question.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think I'm done.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Roberts.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Minister Ayres, your government, the Albanese-Bowen government, endorsed this project when you came to power. You had the authority of the Public Service. You had the whole Public Service at your disposal and you did not do a proper evaluation. The project came out from the Liberals with no policy basis and no options, no alternatives, no business case and no cost-benefit analysis, and it went ahead with no adequate drilling. You knew all of that. You had been sweating on that for years, and yet you still went ahead with it. That's worse than the Liberals. The Liberals went ahead with it because they were ignorant, but you went ahead with it deliberately. Why?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It's a project of national importance. Mr Taylor said in October 2019—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Why did you? My question is: why did you?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
He said:

… we made our investment decision after we'd done a cost benefit, and after we'd done the feasibility work.

That's what Mr Taylor said.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Heavily redacted.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, no.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, it was.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It's the words that he used in a radio interview.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: But you knew all this. You knew all this.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: He said, 'Snowy 2.0 is a defining project in our country's history.'

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: This was authorised under your government, Minister.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The problem for the Liberals and Nationals is they can't accept responsibility for what they got wrong.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You can't accept the facts. It went off the rails under your banner.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: And we will see—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You renegotiated the contract—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson, I've asked you—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: and the whole thing has gone off the rails.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Henderson, I've asked you a number of times to please stop interjecting while the minister is answering Senator Roberts's questions.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You may be unable to accept responsibility—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: You can't accept the facts, Minister.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: and you demonstrate that when you shout over the top of me. This is an important project that was set up badly by the previous government. The costs of abandoning it are immense for the Australian community. We will see it through, and we will get it done, and we are relying upon Snowy Hydro to do that work. It is, as Mr Taylor said, an important project.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What work, Minister, has your government done since 2022, when it came into power and knew this was a dog, was very badly set up and was very badly managed? It was a mess. What extra work did you do to satisfy yourselves that it was a good project? This is now your project. You've had four bloody years to do it and you've just gone from mess to mess. What extra work did you do? What extra analysis? What did you do to correct the Liberals' mistakes?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Barnes will be able to talk to the engagement between the government and Snowy Hydro to make sure that the work required to get this, in an engineering and business and commercial sense, through from one end to the other, literally, is done in the most efficient and effective way possible. It started in a pretty bad place with an unfunded, uncosted project that had, as Mr Barnes has said and I think has been observed by experts, a weakness in terms of its engineering design.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Why didn't you cancel it when you first came to power? Why didn't you do your due diligence? You're telling us how bad these people were, and you just accepted that you rubber stamped it blindly.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Them and Mr Joyce, of course, who was engaged in this work too.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Why didn't you stop this project? Why didn't you review the project?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Because, like with so many things, we had to clean up the Liberals' messes. That's what we had to do.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Cleaning it up could mean shutting it up.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: That's what we have to do.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What due diligence did you do before you decided it was too important? What specifically did you do? This is on you. It started as a mess, that's true, but this is on you. You could have shut it down in 2022.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd

Absolutely not. The original contract didn't have the provisions that would normally be required for penalties for contractors missing cost and performance targets. The problem is this was an Angus Taylor blank cheque. That's how this began. Now, what's changed since we've taken government—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: As Mr Barnes was at pains to go through, characterising this as a cost-plus contract is completely inaccurate. It's a phrase that is used for completely partisan purposes and deliberately misunderstands the nature of the contract, the reason that having that kind of oversight engaged in the contract is so important and why the way Mr Taylor set this up was so deficient. Every time Mr Taylor was taken to these issues, he ignored the risks. Every time he became aware of the risks, he covered them up. Australians did not know the true state of this project until we took government. It is an important project. We are going to get it done. We are very disappointed with the increase in costs, and you have Mr Barnes here in a position able to answer questions in detail about the work he is on. For example, the power station excavation, which hadn't even started at the time of the reset, is now almost 90 per cent complete. Tunnelling, bricks and mortar, plant and equipment—real progress, the way that I would measure it in the real world, is being made. It's hard work that 5,000 Australians are engaged in, and I'm not going to talk down their efforts for a second.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Roberts.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Mr Barnes is going to answer, isn't he?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What's the question, sorry?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What I put to Senator Ayres. What have you done? Why did you continue the project?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text:
If I can give you a little bit of a chronology. In early 2022—so before my time, but I was able to review the records—the project was making in the order of 0.2 per cent progress per month. The contractor was needing propping up with a cashflow support agreement, and there were $4 billion of claims on the table. Fixed-price contracts tend to drive an adversarial approach where you don't get progress. The first question that is asked when one encounters a problem is: how does this get paid for, because it's not our fault? The project was not moving forward.

In 2023 we moved it to an incentivised target cost model, which has rewards and penalties for performance. Those are very common across Australia; in fact, in the last few years, they are probably the dominant form of construction contract. That allows you to have an open conversation about making progress on the project. In 2023, the advice of myself and the Snowy board—just to be clear, it's myself and the Snowy board that do the work—was to reset this contract to an ITC model and get progress moving again, and we saw progress double over that period.

What we underestimated at the time, and what we got wrong—and I'm not shying away from that—was that we relied on the contractor's estimate for the balance of the work. In the middle of 2023 we were $4.3 billion through the job, on which the contractor received no margin. At that point the contractor estimated the balance of the job, and that was wrong. We saw that early, and we were clear—I think it was October 2025 when we announced that we would not be able to complete this project for $12 billion. We are making sure that the design immaturity that was enduring is corrected, and that's what we've corrected in the last year. In the last year we've had great progress on all the excavation work. I've explained what we got wrong in that estimation process, and I've explained where I think the project will end.

To come to the value of Snowy 2.0, clearly Snowy Hydro is a profit-making organisation. This is a unique asset in a market that does not yet exist. It's dealing with a range of scenarios for this asset. Earlier in the year we released a report by Baringa Partners which showed what the grid looked like with and without Snowy 2.0. Without Snowy 2.0, reliability is put at risk and prices are higher. We did the counterfactual to eight-hour batteries, which are currently the largest commercial alternative to Snowy 2.0, and one would have had to have 42,000 megawatts of eight-hour batteries. The current cost of that would be over $80 billion. From my perspective and the Snowy Hydro board's perspective, we've got the right contract model to make progress. This project is incredibly valuable to the grid, and the risks of not doing it would risk reliability and higher prices in the electricity market. We're committed to this project. The Snowy Hydro board and I provided advice to government a few weeks ago of the new cost range and that the project should continue.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you. Another part of the project is to assess not just the cost but the risk. What have you done since you came on board, and what has the Albanese-Bowen government done, since it took power in this country, to understand the risks better? What geophysical drilling have you done at the front of the tunnels?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Snowy Hydro is responsible for delivering this project. The first thing we did was to get transparency and visibility and a contract model that worked. We could not have done the work we've done under a fixed-price model, I can assure you; that $4 billion would be $20 billion, and we'd be in court, and the project would not be moving forward. We have a very rigorous cost verification process. We have a number of independent experts embedded within the contractors' team and our own team. We are adding independent advice to the Snowy board.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What have you done to reduce the risk? That's the biggest thing in this project.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Unfortunately, once the project is sanctioned and you've started digging holes and drilling tunnels, you've lost the opportunity to do broad geological surveying.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Can't you do that ahead of the drilling machine, to at least clarify that?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: For the areas that we are concerned about, the famous TBM Florence is currently ahead of a naturally occurring asbestos zone, and there's drilling ahead of the machine to deal with that. TBM Monica, which will traverse the Long Plain Fault Zone, has subsequently had full length of the drive geological surveying—so that's the full couple of kilometres where we think this zone is tricky. The new tunnel boring machine that we acquired to deal with the Long Plain Fault Zone—which by the way, would not have been a decision you would have made under a fixed-price contract; you would have let poor old Florence get there and fail, and would have many years of delay. TBM Monica has got the most advanced probe in technology, along with dewatering technology to prepare the ground ahead. There's a lot of governance oversight and there are a lot of physical things we've done on the ground to assure ourselves we can continue to get this job to move. The team in Snowy that's responsible for this—at the time of the reset it was maybe 30 or 40 people. I now have 200 people embedded on this project.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What's the net present value now of this project?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We haven't released the business case at this point, because the job to date was to get advice to government to work out the subsequent support.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Still no business case?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We have done a range of economic modelling both on the cost range and the return range, and that will inform the government support over the next few months.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What will it cost total—I think it's now $22 billion estimated, plus contingencies—and what will it save per year with the miniscule amount of electricity it's going to produce per year?

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Snowy 2.0 does a number of things. The first thing is it absorbs excess renewables. If you read some reports out of the UK recently about the massively escalating cost of what they call turndown payments—so when a wind farm or solar farm can't produce because the demand is not there, because the—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Which we told everyone about.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Snowy 2.0 is fantastic at absorbing that excess production. That allows 6,000 to 7,000 megawatts of wind farms and solar farms to be developed. So that's point No. 1, that it brings cheap energy to the grid. Point No. 2 is that Snowy 2.0 then stores that energy for periods when demand is higher, in the evening. More importantly, when we get two or three days, or up to a week, of low wind and solar production, the grid does not solve without Snowy 2.0 in those circumstances. It then provides system strength services. So when the big coal plants retire and the big spinning machines are not there, Snowy 2.0 will provide that service. In addition to that, the effect on wholesale prices is to reduce those because we are not bringing on what might be more expensive gas or overinvesting in batteries and renewables to provide that service. Then the final one, which does not accrue to Snowy Hydro of course, is the broad economic benefits through the construction phase

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It seems ludicrous to me that you compare batteries, because batteries are not industrial scale. You also have admitted there are out-of-peak periods that are out of sync with demand, so we are going to plunge $50 billion into this mess just to overcome an inherent flaw in solar and wind. What's wrong with just building a coal-fired power station? You could be done with it.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: My job as CEO of Snowy Hydro is to power Australia's renewable energy future. That's in our statement of expectation, and that's what Snowy 2.0 will do.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: As an adviser in 2017, I called for the project to be scrapped. As a senator, on 25 October 2023—three years ago—I called for it to be scrapped. At the time, sunk cost was only $4 billion against a project cost of $12 billion. Minister, in your pursuit of an ideological goal, net zero, that other countries are moving away from, your government has wasted $12 billion on this foolhardy project and wants to waste another $40 billion including transmission lines which were never imagined to be needed. And who knows how much there will be in interest payments over the next 30 years? We haven't got a figure on that. Minister, will you put this idiot idea out of its misery and get back to building baseload power generation.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, I wouldn't use that kind of language to describe the people and the project that is going on here. It's an important project for Australia. The previous government—and I'm sharply critical of their failure to plan—recognised this was an important project for the country. The alternative, as you say, is wall-to-wall outdated technology being installed to take Australia backwards, lift our costs, make us uncompetitive and force industry offshore. Installing coal-fired power, which appears to be your alternative proposition—

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The footprint is incredibly small and there's high energy density.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I listened patiently to what you said, even though I sharply disagree with it—all of it. I don't want to be interrupted; I didn't interrupt you. Your prescription—Senator Hanson's prescription and Mr Joyce's prescription—for the country is to take us backwards, to lift our costs, to force industry offshore and to take us to lower growth, lower employment and a lower wages future. I understand that's what you want to do, but that's not what the Albanese government is going to do. We're going to finish this project because it's in the national interest to finish it. Now, you'll have to put up with, over the course of the next short while, Senator Watt, who's going to be delighted to—

portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd

The second point is Australia has a different geography to other countries. So our relative competitive advantage is different to other countries.

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd

agency: Snowy Hydro Ltd
