text: Thank you for appearing tonight. Thank you for your answer to question on notice SQ26-446, which shows that the median age of the 170 active mining and resource projects waiting for environmental approval is 116 weeks. That's the median.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: An answer to a question on notice. An average age of 186 weeks suggests a small number of projects have been waiting more than three years for approval. Do you have a program of evaluating each of these delayed approvals and facilitating a resolution?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It would be the case that there would be some resources projects that take a long time to assess, and it would also be the case that there would be some that take not very long at all. That all depends on the level of environmental impact and the proponent participation in the process as well as the EPA's management of those processes. Perhaps Mr Bradley or his officials can talk to you about the management of those sorts of referrals.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It is certainly a priority to make sure that we move projects through the system as much as possible. We look at not only the average but also the aged cases. What we have found is that, in the last four years, we've managed to see 60 per cent of all projects manage their impacts to levels below significant. This is in terms of all projects, collectively. In the case of fossil fuel projects, we have been monitoring some of those that are older. In terms of aged cases, we've got seven projects that are still listed on the system that are over 10 years old. In each of those seven cases, the matter is in the hands of the proponent to come back with further information. Sometimes, we find that the circumstances of the proponent and the additional information that's required will lead to a project ageing while it's on our books, but we do actively manage it. As we were saying earlier, we've found that, since the commencement of the National EPA, we've seen 63 projects greenlit, and we've seen 93 per cent of those within the statutory timeframe.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority

text: I have to get a chance to get these questions in. They go to the Adelaide Park Lands and the cumulative impact of a range of measures there. Minister Watt, state planning authorities are systematically exploiting internal self-assessments to treat major, interconnected infrastructure developments in our heritage parklands as entirely isolated events. By splitting projects like the Walker Tower, the international commercial golf course that is in North Adelaide Public Golf Course, a 20-metre commercial driving range safety fence in Park 27A and the MotoGP circuit into separate pieces, they deliberately avoid mandatory cumulative impact referrals under the EPBC Act. The cumulative impact of these is really causing enormous concern in Adelaide and South Australia, and it represents death by a thousand cuts for the Adelaide Park Lands. When those individual components are allowed to bypass independent federal audits via fast-tracked internal processes, the overarching spatial integrity of the entire national heritage site is permanently compromised. Why haven't these successive cumulative encroachments on a national heritage site triggered a significant impact under section 15 of the EPBC Act?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Initially, it's probably best if I get the EPA to answer questions about how these applications are being dealt with, and they can answer the direct questions as well.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I might note that, most recently on 18 September, the national EPA received a valid referral from the Department for Infrastructure and Transport of South Australia for the proposed Adelaide Circuit redevelopment project. Indeed, today, the delegate made a referral to—

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Sorry, Mr Bradley, I don't like to interrupt you, but my question was about the cumulative impact. I've got further questions about MotoGP, but I'm asking about the cumulative impact of these measures.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The point I was trying to make is that, in the case that the delegates made the decision today, the delegate has determined that significant impacts are unlikely to occur, including to those national heritage values of the Adelaide Park Lands and the city layout, and other matters, like the grey-headed flying fox. We're certainly aware of a number of development proposals within the parklands and the community concern about cumulative impacts of the proposals, and we'll continue to work with the South Australian government to make sure that there is appropriate consideration of matters of national environmental significance in the parklands, including appropriate impact avoidance and negation measures. We need to look at the individual matters before us, including where we have a referral. The proponent is obliged to refer to us where there is likely to be significant impact on a matter of national environmental significance. They're also able to undertake a self-assessment and are able to consider or conclude, on that self-assessment, that there is unlikely to be a significant impact. In those cases, we'll assess the material before us.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Did you say a decision has been made today?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: A decision has been made today in relation to the MotoGP that the matter will be non-controlled action if undertaken in a particular manner, and there are some requirements there in relation to the particular manner in which it needs to be undertaken.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Can you spell those out.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It was found that it was unlikely to have a significant impact on the grey box threatened ecological community if there were a number of particular manner requirements undertaken. They include limiting the clearance of grey box to 1.1 hectares, the translocation of the grey box threatened ecological community from within the disturbance area to an adjacent area, the installation of temporary fencing during construction works and the installation of permanent fencing after completion of construction around the grey box threatened ecological community.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Has the proponent established what might be the impacts on the highly vulnerable grey-headed flying fox during the race, given that the race will be during the breeding season of this creature, the noise will be extreme at 130 decibels and therefore well outside the normal range, and the northern extent of the race will be quite close to that colony?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The practice would be that the delegate would release a statement of reasons, on request, which would set out all of that material in relation to the delegate's reasoning. But, in short, the delegate did conclude that significant impacts were unlikely to the grey-headed flying fox. It was not one of the matters that required particular measures.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: All of that decision, in full detail, is now public?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: No, sorry. As of today, the decision is public on the portal, and then a statement of reasons is released subsequently.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: How soon?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I might ask Ms Calhoun to comment.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: There has been no request for a statement of reasons at this point, but we do understand the interest in this project, so we are working on a statement of reasons. It's likely to be—

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: There is extreme interest in Adelaide. People care passionately about this issue. There are thousands of citizens out every weekend on this question. There is extreme hostility to what it is proposed to do here and the potential impact. You still haven't dealt, I believe, with the cumulative impact of a range of measures that are significantly transforming the historical nature of these parklands. How are you going to deal with the cumulative nature of these really significant intrusions on the parklands, Minister?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I don't interfere in the way the EPA approaches its decision-making. They may care to explain to you how they take those matters into account.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I think it's best to wait till we have the statement of reasons for this particular consideration, but they are project by project in terms of how they're being referred.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: So they're not cumulative in their assessment. You are looking at a particular development in relation to MotoGP, are you not?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Correct.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It's a real failure that you don't look at the cumulative impact. Minister Watt, the City of Adelaide—the Council—has officially submitted a 12-page statutory deficiency brief to your office regarding the MotoGP track development, explicitly calling out the state government for a total lack of consultation with local community groups. Given the City of Adelaide Council has formally blown the whistle on this total exclusion of the public, will you continue to claim that the national heritage values regarding visual legibility are merely advisory, or will you listen to the community and exercise your statutory call-in powers under section 70 of the EPBC Act to halt the works?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Which project are you talking about there?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm talking about the MotoGP track development.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The City of Adelaide is entitled to their views about community consultation. What the EPA takes into account is whether a referred project is likely to have a significant impact on nationally protected matters, and you've heard from the EPA as to what decision they reached on that.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: If I could add to that: we do, as part of the referral assessment, undertake public consultation. Between 18 September and 2 October, we received over 300 comments on the referral as part of that mandatory public consultation period and considered each of those comments as part of the delegate's decision I referred to earlier.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Can you confirm whether this project was assessed against the impact on the national heritage value of the Adelaide Park Lands of a permanent new infrastructure project on this masterwork of urban design, or was it from a purely environmental standpoint?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I can confirm that the delegate did consider the national heritage values of the Adelaide Park Lands and city layout as part of the protected matters to be considered and concluded that it was unlikely to have a significant impact.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The referral explicitly excludes the annual MotoGP event from the EPBC assessment, despite it being the reason for the track redevelopment. Such an event will bring with it further environmental impacts, which include the impacts of hosting a three-day race event over a whole weekend, installation and removal of very significant works, and temporary facilities which include curbing, gravel traps and internal access tracks. Will the South Australian Motor Sport Board be required to submit another referral so that the EPA can assess the environmental impacts of such works and the event itself?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: To be explicit, the referral that was assessed by the delegate did consider both the environmental matters I referred to earlier, particularly the Grey Box threatened ecological community and the grey-headed flying fox. They were the significant environmental considerations in that process, but it also considered the national heritage values of the Adelaide Park Lands and city layout. It has considered those heritage matters.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: But you haven't considered the actual impact of the three-day race itself, have you?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I don't believe so.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It was the works, not the actual race.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: My understanding is that it was the works, but I'd need to look at the referral document.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Will you assess the event itself?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It does actually exclude the event. We are actively working with the South Australian government to determine both the cumulative impacts on the Adelaide Parklands and what actions need to be referred. If they determine that they believe a matter should be referred to us, it will be. We're having discussions. They understand what the requirements are. This has been referred, and they will determine if the next stage requires consideration by us through a referral.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: What opportunity will there be in that consideration for the voice and consultation with South Australian citizens?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: If it were referred to us, for instance, there would be that public consultation period. It's on the proponent to determine whether they think it will be a matter that has an impact on MNES and at that point in time it would go through our normal process, which has a number of phases for public consultation.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I want you to know how incredibly disappointed many South Australian citizens will be about today's decision. It is a historic attack on a really important facility, a magnificent urban design. It has really been significantly reshaped by the cumulative impact, which your consideration does not allow true assessment of. Little piece by little piece, it's a magnificent park that is transformed over time by a thousand cuts.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator Thorpe?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm asking about the forestry agreement between the Commonwealth and the Tasmanian government. I'll start with you, Minister. You are currently negotiating a draft bilateral approval agreement for forestry with the Tasmanian government. By now, we were supposed to have a First Nations engagement standard under the national environment reforms. I think it's been about six years that we've been waiting for that. You've produced a guide, but—given that there's no First Nations engagement standard, it's taking years to get that together, you're putting all the other standards before the most important one and we were meant to be first but are being kicked down the road again—will you guarantee that there will be no bilateral agreement that does not put the principle of free, prior and informed consent of the traditional owners at the forefront of any assessment of proposed forestry actions?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Just to correct a couple of things there, I don't know that anyone made a commitment that a First Nations engagement standard for the EPBC would be the first standard that we would create. Certainly, I've never given that commitment.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Your predecessor did.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'm not sure about that. As I've explained previously, the reason we haven't yet completed a First Nations engagement standard is that we are also undertaking reform to the cultural heritage laws, which we've discussed. It's the intention as part of those reforms to develop a standard related to that piece of legislation. We need to do those two pieces of work together. In the period of time that we don't have a First Nations engagement standard, if you like, the way that First Nations engagement will be monitored or regulated, whichever word you want to use, is through the more general community engagement standard that has been created. I realise that's not the same, and I'm trying to remember whether there were specific references to engagement with First Nations people in the community engagement standard. One of the officials might be able to help me with that. But community engagement in general will need to follow what's set out in that standard. I accept that's not the same as a First Nations engagement standard.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Good luck getting blackfellas to that one, then, given the state of the nation. That's why we do that—so we create a safe space and that we're talking to people where we're nowhere safe and we can get a seat at the table. If it's a general discussion or a general consultation, blackfellas are put down the back every time, so it won't work, and you know that.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: It was always our intention to have a First Nations engagement standard finalised by now. The work on cultural heritage reform has taken longer than we would have liked. And it is important that those two pieces of work happen together. Mr Manning might be able to add something here.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The community engagement standard will apply to the arrangement that we accredit in Tasmania, and that's where that will actually kick into that process. I think your question went to the consultations that will occur in terms of our negotiations with Tasmania leading towards the making of that agreement, putting that arrangement in place. There are statutory and other consultation processes which are set out in the act that we need to go through in order to put that arrangement in place. They will include a public consultation process on the draft bilateral agreement that we're working towards having ready for that process in the not-too-distant future. I'd have to check. I think there might be another one closer towards the end, but don't hold me to that at the moment. I guess where I'm going with this is that, whilst at the moment we are very much focused on the negotiations in relation to the terms of that bilateral agreement with Tasmania, we will in due course—and I don't expect it's too far away—turn our minds to what the public consultation process for that will look like. That's where we will, in conjunction with our Tasmanian colleagues, look at how we make sure that the whole process gets commented upon by all of the stakeholders who have an interest in it, including First Nations Australians.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Who's on the taskforce to negotiate the bilateral agreement?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Who is on the taskforce? From our side?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Who's on the taskforce in general? Who are the players?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Within the department, we have established a taskforce in order to work on this RFA transition arrangement, and we're working on that with the three relevant states. That sits within my division. Ms Purcell here is the branch head responsible for the RFA taskforce. We have a team of people who work with us in relation to that. In Tasmania, they have established similar arrangements that involve the relevant players—the department down there, Building Tasmania, the Forest Practices Authority, Sustainable Timber Tasmania et cetera, the relevant government agencies—and they have a team there who are working with us to negotiate that agreement.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Traditional owners have asked for specific First Nations community briefings but were rebuked and told they can just be part of the wider consultation. Meanwhile, there have been dedicated briefings with the forest industry. The traditional owners are obviously not like anyone else and we're certainly not destroying our land; we're trying to protect it for all of you people. Why is a dedicated briefing being denied to the—

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I wasn't aware of that, Senator Thorpe. We'll have a look at that. It is the case that the department has met with representatives of the forestry industry. They have also met with representatives of environment groups in Tasmania.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Yes, but they're not the traditional owners.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I know that.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: The minister is right, we've held industry briefing sessions—I think 10, according to my count. Looking at the NGO and other stakeholder sessions, I think we've held a total of 14 of those thus far across the process in Tasmania. Ms Purcell and I were down there not that long ago. We met with a range of NGOs and that included some First Nations people as part of that. We've been seeking to take meetings whenever people approach us. There's been no rebuking of anyone from my perspective.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, that's not what they're telling me. That's why I'm asking the question. I'll put the rest on notice, but I do have to quickly ask about Djab Wurrung. Another section 18 has been put in. We're talking about ancient birthing trees—over 800 years old, older than the colony, before the invaders came. Djab Wurrung trees were used for birthing. They were culturally modified to allow families to be in the tree, protected from the weather and to deliver babies. So my ancestors' blood is in that beautiful part of the country, and we have Djab Wurrung people being arrested. Forty cops from Melbourne in riot cars rocked up while we were trying to protect these beautiful trees and the landscape around it. Can I ask where the section 18 notice that you received on 20 October is at so that no more people are arrested, and we can protect our place of worship? Because if it was a place of worship in a colonisers mind, this wouldn't be happening. Please tell me what's going on with Djab Wurrung.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: We do have a section 18 application for protection of trees at Djab Wurrung that is currently under assessment.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Under assessment. Have Djab Wurrung trees and that landscape area been a problem for this government since youse arrived? Because this has been on the table for a long time—since I've been here, in fact.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I don't know about that history. What I am aware of is that an application was made about eight or six days ago, and that's now being considered by the department.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: And that's it?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Well, that's what we do.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: How long is the process? There are trees being cut down now. The security guards are allegedly poisoning the trees as well. So there are a whole lot of problems going on there. Until a decision is made at this level, it will continue to happen. There are also Nazis not far, so it's a very problematic issue for this government, which needs to be addressed as a matter of urgency because people's lives and sacred birthing trees are at risk. So can you tell me how long that's going to take?

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Senator, I can't give you a hard date on how long it will take to do the assessment. What I can tell you is that, in doing the assessment, we will need to consider the cultural significance in accordance with tradition, the threat or harm that is being defined in that application and the urgency that's within that application. Once we have all of that information, we are able to undertake the assessment and make a determination.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: I'll have it to you tomorrow. Thank you so much.

agency: National Environmental Protection Authority
portfolio: CLIMATE CHANGE, ENERGY, THE ENVIRONMENT AND WATER PORTFOLIO
text: Thank you to all. That concludes today's hearing. Thank you to all witnesses who appeared and to Hansard and Broadcasting for their assistance. The committee has agreed that responses to questions on notice should be provided by COB, close of business, 17 December 2026. I remind senators that the committee has agreed that any written questions on notice should be lodged with the secretariat by 5 November 2026. I thank all participants in today's hearing and my colleagues for their assistance. The committee stands adjourned.
